#1861. Mauricio Pochettino 'agrees to be new Manchester United manager' after overnight talks

Manchester United are reportedly finalising an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has been identified as the club’s first-choice candidate to replace Michael Carrick, who is set to be sacked.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have flown out to meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, where he resides and company INEOS have offices in the principality.

Carrick is expected to again take charge of a depleted first-team training session at Carrington today, while work is concluding on hiring his replacement.

According to The Athletic, United spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Pochettino’s representatives, with no major obstacles expected and a final agreement expected.

The Guardian reported on Tuesday evening that Pochettino was keen to become the next Man Utd manager.

However, the club have yet to approach US Soccer, who would be entitled to around $10m (£7.4m) in compensation through an exit clause in the Argentine’s contract.

Pochettino, currently in charge of the United States national team, is contracted until 2030 but is reportedly keen to take the Old Trafford job. His coaching staff would also require compensation if he leaves.

According to iNews, Pochettino was heavily backed by the Glazer family to replace Carrick in the Man Utd dugout.

The Glazers had stepped back from direct involvement in footballing decisions since selling shares to Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS investment, but it appears the family are set for a more active role after further regression on the pitch.

Pochettino looks set to beat out-of-work Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann for the job.

Director of football Wilcox is said to favour a manager with a track record in the Premier League, with Howe and then Pochettino of interest, while head of recruitment Christopher Vivell is keen on restarting a relationship with Nagelsmann, the pair working together at RB Leipzig.

The former Southampton, Chelsea, and Tottenham boss has previously spoken about his desire to return to the Premier League and previous Manchester United interest in his services.

It could be a case of third time lucky for Pochettino, who missed out on the Man Utd job in 2018 and 2022 to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag, respectively.

A deal may not be straightforward, however. As it is the international break, Pochettino is set to take charge of a USA double-header against Haiti.

Further complications arise from the fact that the Argentine coach is currently into the first months of a new four-year deal with the USA national team.

Compensation would also need to be worked out for his coaching staff, who are expected to cross the pond with Pochettino to take up the role.

#1860. Manchester United recruitment team should be ‘sacked’ over £50m transfer, says Jamie Redknapp

Jamie Redknapp says Andrey Santos is ‘not a Manchester United player’ and claims whoever was responsible for his signing ‘deserves the sack’.

Desperate for midfield reinforcements over the summer, United spent £50m to sign Brazil international Santos from Premier League rivals Chelsea.

Manchester United made midfield targets their priority after Casemiro left Old Trafford and Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious injury at the World Cup.

Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans joined Michael Carrick’s squad on top of Santos but all three midfielders have made inauspicious starts to their United careers.

Santos has earned just seven starts for a Manchester United team sitting in the relegation zone heading into the international break.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Redknapp doubts the 22-year-old Brazilian is at the level required to play for United and says bringing him to the club was a ‘sackable offence’ by those in charge at Old Trafford.

‘Can I throw one player at you? And this is no disrespect to the boy, because he’s not a bad player, but whoever brought in Andrey Santos, that for me is a sackable offence,’ Redknapp said on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Vegas.

‘He is not a Manchester United player. He’s a decent player, he’s okay. But they brought [Youri] Tielemans in just after it.

‘What makes them think, “Okay, I’m going to get two midfield players”, when I’ve got [Kobbie] Mainoo there – three very similar players that haven’t got any athleticism to get round the pitch?’

When it was point to him that Manchester United’s director of recruitment Christopher Vivell knew Santos from his previous spell at Chelsea, Redknapp added: ‘Even worse, then. I’d let them off the hook if they didn’t know him.’

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has also criticised Manchester United’s pursuit of Santos, who made just 47 appearances for Chelsea.

‘I’m not sure Andrey Santos was the right signing for Manchester United at £50m,’ Gerrard said last month.

‘I just think to play in Manchester United’s midfield every single game, every single weekend, you’d expect to compete for the Premier League and the Champions League.

‘Santos, he’s a good player, but for me, he’s not a Manchester United player. I think he’s a bit short, that would be my opinion. United’s midfield is way off the level, it’s way off.’

United’s dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign looks set to cost former England midfielder Carrick his job at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino, the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss, is the frontrunner to take over at Manchester United.

If appointed, Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils would be a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool after the international break.

#1858. Turkey vs Belgium - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 17:50, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 22:34

Seeking to strengthen their hopes of qualifying for the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Belgium travel to Gursel Aksel Stadium in Izmir to face Turkey in their penultimate League A Group 1 fixture on Thursday evening.

While the hosts’ fate is all but sealed, the visitors currently sit third in the group and are playing catch up behind both France and Italy heading into their remaining two matches this week.

After finishing third in their group behind both France and Italy in the 2024-25 Nations League, Belgium are at risk of suffering the same fate this year having won two and lost two of their opening four matches in League A.

The September/October international break was the first time the Red Devils were in action under new head coach Mark van Bommel, who saw “beautiful things” from his players despite suffering a heavy 4-1 defeat to France on matchday four.

Sitting one point behind Italy and four adrift of leaders France, Belgium know that a defeat in Turkey and an Azzurri win over Les Bleus would end their hopes of securing a top-two finish in the group. However, collecting three points on Thursday would ensure that the group will be decided on the final matchday.

Ranked eighth in the world by FIFA, Belgium will take comfort from having already beaten both Turkey and Italy in the Nations League without reply, winning 2-0 away against the latter before beating the former 3-0 on home soil courtesy of a Kevin De Bruyne brace and a strike from record goalscorer Romelu Lukaku.

Having lost only one of their last six encounters with Turkey across all competitions, the Red Devils head to Izmir confident of avoiding consecutive international defeats for the first time since March 2025.

Turkey are beginning a new era under former international midfielder Sergen Yalcin, who was appointed head coach last month following the dismissal of Vincenzo Montella after three years in charge.

Montella’s reign came to an end following Turkey’s nightmare start to their Nations League campaign, losing each of their opening four matches by an aggregate score of 11-2; this poor run of form came after they were dumped out in the 2026 World Cup group stage over the summer.

Yalcin returns to management just six months after leaving his role with Besiktas, who finished fourth in the Turkish Super Lig last season. The 54-year-old has called for “unity and togetherness” to ensure that the national team can “experience very successful days from now on”.

Ranked 31st in the world by FIFA, Turkey cannot qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals, but they still have a slim chance of avoiding direct relegation from League A, needing points from their final two matches to edge out Serbia and Czechia as one of the two best fourth-placed teams across all groups in League A.

To avoid finishing rock bottom of the group, Turkey must beat Belgium by at least four goals on Thursday to overtake them on the head-to-head tiebreaker, secure another victory against France on matchday six, and hope Belgium drop points in their final game against Italy.

The Crescent-Stars, who won four consecutive home matches prior to their two Nations League home losses this term, are unbeaten in three meetings with Belgium on their own turf, winning 3-2 in their most recent home encounter in a Euro 2012 qualifier.

Turkey are still having to cope without star attacker Kenan Yildiz, who requires further treatment to a metatarsal fracture at club level with Juventus, while Kerem Akturkoglu, Irfan Kahveci, Samet Akaydin and Altay Bayindir are among those left out of the squad after being called up last month.

Centre-back Abdulkerim Bardakci is suspended for the clash with Belgium, while Zeki Celik, Merih Demiral, Ozan Kabak, Salih Ozcan and Can Yilmaz Uzun are all just one booking away from a ban.

Key creative midfielder Arda Guler, who scored and assisted in Real Madrid's La Liga win over Valencia last weekend, is expected to start in an advanced central role, while 108-cap Hakan Calhanoglu will surpass Tuncay (22) to become Turkey third-highest goalscorer if he finds the net on Thursday.

As for Belgium, goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois continues to take a break from international duty, while Van Bommel has revealed that AC Milan defender Koni De ‌Winter refused to be called up because he was unhappy with his lack of game time last month.

Genk’s Josue Kongolo, 20, has subsequently earned his first senior call-up and will battle with Arthur Theate, Brandon Mechele and Nathan Ngoy for a place in the heart of the defence.

Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia is suspended, while Lukaku, Ngoy, Joaquin Seys, Nicolas Raskin and Dodi Lukebakio are all one yellow card away from a ban.

Midfield stars De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans are both back from a ban they served on matchday four last month, while winger Jeremy Doku has returned to the squad and is likely to start after missing the previous international window through injury.

Cakir; Celik, Kabak, Demiral, Kadioglu; Ozcan, Calhanoglu; Aydin, Guler, Yilmaz; Gul

Lammens; Castagne, Ngoy, Mechele, De Cuyper; Raskin, Tielemans; Lukebakio, De Bruyne, Doku; De Ketelaere

Turkey will be desperate for an immediate manager bounce under Yalcin as they look to kick-start their survival bid, but Belgium are rightfully regarded as favourites following their comfortable three-goal victory over the Crescent-Stars last month.

Boosted by the return of a few key players, the Red Devils should possess enough firepower to breach a leaky Turkish backline and are well-placed to claim three important points on the road.

#1857. Arsenal star addresses January exit rumours as Mikel Arteta talks confirmed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Martin Zubimendi has dismissed speculation that he is close to leaving Arsenal.

The midfielder has not started a Premier League game for the Gunners this season, having fallen behind Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly in the pecking order.

With minutes hard to come by, there have been suggestions that Zubimendi was unhappy and looking for a way out of Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid are among the clubs understood to be monitoring his situation and some reports in Spain have claimed that Zubimendi was nearing a return to his homeland.

However, speaking to Marca while on international duty, the 27-year-old revealed that is “not at all” true.

“To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press,” Zubimendi said.

“I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

“Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

“Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.”

Asked if he will remain at the club until at least the summer, Zubimendi added: “Yes, I hope so. I’m happy there.”

Zubimendi started 33 of Arsenal’s first 34 league matches last season, making a big impact in his first season in England.

However, he dropped out of the side in the final weeks of the campaign as Myles Lewis-Skelly earned Mikel Arteta’s trust in midfield.

Zubimendi’s task has been made tougher this season by the £75million arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, but the Spaniard has not been surprised by his lack of opportunities in the opening months of the campaign.

Arsenal star reveals how Arteta is 'different to any other manager'

When Arsenal youngsters will play for England after double selection boost

“I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season,” Arteta said.

“As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me. He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side

“I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

“I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.”

As well as not starting in the Premier League, Zubimendi has only made two appearances in Europe. One of those was an eight-minute cameo against Napoli.

However, he insisted: “I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

“Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

“I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

“I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.”

#1854. Commentators haven't the foggiest idea what's going on: Thick mist ruins FA Cup clash for TV viewers - and fans use phone torches to see the action!

Published: 16:25 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 16:27 EST, 7 November 2026

'Peak FA Cup', was the verdict from TV viewers watching (or trying to watch) the clash between Notts County and Altrincham as thick fog obscured the action.

Those tuning in on TNT Sports were baffled by what was actually happening in the game when the mist descended at Moss Lane.

Commentators saw the funny side, with Adam Summerton chuckling, saying: 'Your guess is as good as mine at the minute,' when asked by his partner what was going on.

As the match progressed, the foggy conditions only worsened and it became difficult for the players to see far in front of them, let alone those trying to spectate in the ground and at home.

Even though the conditions appeared to simply be deep fog, one local claimed it was smoke from local firework parties causing the white-out.

They wrote: 'It is smoke from the bonfire night fireworks and bonfires. I live round the corner, it is literally just smoke. All you can smell in the air is smoke.'

The fog is closing in at Moss Lane! 🌫️Conditions are getting tricky for Altrincham and Notts County 👀📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/gTM9e3KA2w

Fog descended on the FA Cup clash between Altrincham and Notts County and TV viewers could hardly tell what was going on

Fans pulled out the torches on their phones in a light-hearted bid to see more of the action

Despite the lack of quality action for fans to watch at Moss Lane, plenty of them saw the funny side and even took out their phone torches in unison to try and cut through the gloom.

Those at home poked fun at the scene, with one posting: 'Can you ask the ref that if it goes to pens they bring the goal closer to the cameras so we can watch them?'

Another wrote: 'Where's the orange ball? I miss those days!'

Not everyone could see the humour in the situation, with one user on X writing: 'I'm sorry but this is ridiculous it should be abandoned. You could be miles offside.'

The game itself went to penalties, which caused further problems for the commentators, who had to largely base their reactions on the crowd directly behind the goal.

Ultimately, Notts County survived a scare from the non-league outfit and won 3-2 in the shootout.

Rosaire Longelo netted the final spot-kick to fire the Magpies into the second round of the FA Cup.

They'd had to fight back from 2-1 down in normal time after Lucas Weaver and then Lewis Banks put Altrincham in front.

Callum Roberts scored to make it 2-2 and neither side could find a winner in extra-time, meaning an already memorable game was settled in a fitting and dramatic fashion.

#1853. Mauricio Pochettino's USA contract clause explained as Manchester United finalise deal

Manchester United have finally decided to sack Michael Carrick, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to be the new man in the Old Trafford job.

Reports emerged on Monday evening that a decision has been made to dismiss the under-pressure boss with the club in the Premier League relegation zone.

As many of the squad fly out for international duty with their respective nations, Carrick remains at the training ground to oversaw a depleted first-team group while work continues on finalising a deal to appoint Pochettino

The Athletic report that talks with Pochettino’s representatives began on Tuesday, and BBC Sport add that the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager is ready to accept a job offer.

But, before any announcement, Pochettino must be bought out of his contract with US Soccer.

Pochettino has not been involved in club management since his decision to leave Chelsea, by mutual contest, two and a half years ago.

The Argentine had spent just one year in west London, and was soon after lured by the USA national team to guide them into their home World Cup where they were knocked out at the last-16 stage.

Pochettino was heavily linked with a return to Tottenham before the World Cup, and was widely expected to leave the USMNT setup after the tournament.

However, in August, Pochettino signed a new contract to guide the national team into the 2030 World Cup.

But, with Man Utd now knocking, Pochettino is ready to head back to the Premier League.

#1850. Arsenal get new penalty review after controversial Liverpool decision

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty in their home defeat by Arsenal earlier this month, according to the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel (KMI).

The five-person panel ruled that referee Andy Madley should have given a spot-kick for Jurrien Timber’s first-half shirt pull on Alexander Isak, which prevented the Reds striker from heading a Bradley Barcola cross inside the Arsenal box.

No foul was given and VAR Stuart Attwell did not recommend a review after deciding that there was not enough in the action to overturn the on-field decision, leaving Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola and captain Virgil van Dijk both bemused as well as fans and pundits alike.

Liverpool went on to lose the match 1-0 as a result of Kai Havertz’s early goal, which secured Arsenal’s first top-flight win at Anfield since 2012 as they went back to the top of the table.

The incident sparked a debate over whether players should have to go down in order to get a penalty, with much made of the fact that Isak stayed on his feet despite the contact from Timber.

"The Alex one is a clear penalty," Iraola said after the game. "You hold the shirt, we can all see that he holds the shirt. Because he doesn't go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty. I don't understand it.

"That's the problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor. The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

"It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it."

Iraola responded “yes, definitely” when asked if he would tell Isak to go down next time.

A frustrated Van Dijk said: “I think it was a clear penalty. I've seen it back, and I've seen it being given. It wasn't meant to be. We have 50 cameras.

“Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras? Everyone has seen it. In the end, it wasn't given, and we lost the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal.”

#1849. Why Pochettino’s pressing style could suit Man Utd and what stands in the way

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 18:12

Manchester United face another decision that could define their season. After a disastrous start to the Premier League, with the team in the relegation zone and winless in eight games, Michael Carrick has lost support inside the club. The hierarchy is weighing a change at the top, and according to the English press, Mauricio Pochettino is the leading candidate to take over.

The possibility carries both opportunity and urgency. The Argentinian manager is in charge of the United States national team, but he has a contract clause that would allow him to leave in return for financial compensation. He also knows the Premier League deeply and has come close to taking the United job on other occasions. At 54, he combines experience at high-pressure clubs, rebuilding projects and a style of play that could, in theory, give the Red Devils a clearer identity. That does not mean he is an automatic solution.

Carrick’s situation has deteriorated quickly. After a vote of confidence from the hierarchy, he was given three more games to change the picture. The result was not enough, as United won only once in that period and reached eight games without a Premier League victory. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday kept the team in the relegation zone and increased the pressure for a decision.

On Tuesday, the situation was not officially settled. Sky Sports reported that the hierarchy was carrying out a full performance review, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, and intended to decide Carrick’s future before the end of the international break. ESPN named Pochettino as the board’s preferred candidate if a dismissal goes ahead.

The Argentinian is not new to the club. He has been interviewed for the job on three previous occasions and was among the top names considered in selection processes that ended with other appointments. In an interview with FourFourTwo in May, Pochettino acknowledged that United had shown repeated interest but said the ideal opportunity never materialised.

There is, however, an important contractual question. In August, after the World Cup, Pochettino signed a renewal with the United States Soccer Federation that extends his deal to 2030. According to The Athletic, there is an exit clause of around $10m (about £7.5m). The mechanism would allow an interested club to trigger the clause by paying the compensation. The figure would not necessarily cover the whole coaching staff, however. Pochettino has worked for many years with trusted staff such as assistant Jesus Perez, and releasing those members could push up the cost.

It is also important to understand the scale of the commitment he made to the United States. The renewal was not simply an extension to lead the team at the next World Cup: the federation announced that Pochettino and his team would have a wider role in developing the sport in the country, including youth categories, coach education and technical structure.

Tactically, there are reasons why the name appeals to United. Pochettino built his reputation in England at Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur, teams that combined high pressing, intensity without the ball and vertical attacks. At Tottenham in particular, he turned a young squad into a competitive team that challenged for domestic honours and reached the 2019 Champions League final.

His model usually starts from a 4-2-3-1 or a 4-3-3. In build-up, the centre-backs split, the holding midfielders offer passing lines and the full-backs advance to provide width. The aim is to create numerical superiority in certain areas, draw the opposition press and find space to progress. In attack, the wingers can leave the touchline and occupy inside channels, while the full-backs provide depth on the outside.

The most recognisable feature is the way he defends. Pochettino likes aggressive teams that press the opposition build-up and try to win the ball back quickly after losing it. For that, he needs players able to repeat efforts, close space and keep distances between the lines.

That principle could be interesting for United, who have struggled to find a consistent identity. The Red Devils have more possession, but do not necessarily turn that control into dominance. They have also shown problems sustaining a high block: when the first press is beaten, a lack of mobility and coordination between midfield and defence opens space for the opposition.

Pochettino could offer an answer. Instead of relying on individual moments of pressing, United would have a more defined model to guide the movement of the attackers, the cover of the midfielders and the positioning of the defensive line. There is a condition, however: the squad must be compatible with the manager’s physical demands. He does not usually compromise on commitment without the ball and has shown, in different jobs, a willingness to sideline players who cannot keep up with the intensity he wants. United have players with suitable characteristics, but also imbalances in important areas.

Pochettino has a track record that could help with another aspect of the crisis: squad management. At Tottenham, he worked with a squad that mixed experienced players and rising youngsters, developing names such as Harry Kane and Dele Alli. He also valued homegrown players and built an environment of collective demand. At Southampton, he helped consolidate a competitive team with players who were still establishing themselves.

That ability to develop young players fits one of United’s historic characteristics. The club has a tradition of backing academy talent, but needs to turn that principle into a coherent sporting policy and not just an occasional solution for difficult moments.

His profile also involves demands for intensity and discipline. He is not a manager known for building relationships around names or status. Even so, calling this a guarantee that he will impose order at Old Trafford would oversimplify the problem. A manager’s firm hand only produces lasting effects when there is backing from the hierarchy and a structure that supports his decisions.

That is where the biggest doubt lies over a possible appointment. United have gone through successive changes of manager, sporting project and transfer strategy. The current crisis did not arise only from Carrick’s tactical choices: the squad has imbalances, the board has to set priorities and the club is still searching for stability in how football is run.

Pochettino’s experience at Chelsea also recommends caution. In London, he improved the team’s performance and finished sixth in the 2023-24 Premier League, but did not stay in the job to continue the project. In Paris, he won the French league title with Paris Saint-Germain, but struggled to balance a squad full of stars and meet the club’s European expectations.

United need a manager who can stabilise the team in the short term and at the same time set a direction for the future. Pochettino has Premier League experience, knows the pressure of running a club with a huge fanbase and offers a playing proposal that could give the team an identity. It is not a baseless bet. He could be a sporting solution that makes sense. What is still unclear is whether United are ready to provide the conditions he needs to succeed.

#1848. Tuchel confirms Kane will win record-breaking 126th England cap versus Croatia

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Harry Kane will win his record-breaking 126th England cap against Croatia, Thomas Tuchel has confirmed, with the Three Lions' boss anticipating a "beautiful occasion".

Kane's next England outing will see him write his name into the record books, as he surpasses Peter Shilton (125) outright as his country's all-time leading appearance-maker.

The Bayern Munich striker has long been England's all-time leading scorer, having surpassed Wayne Rooney's record in March 2023, reaching 91 international goals since then.

And Kane's landmark appearance will come on home soil at Wembley Stadium on Thursday, on the same night that he presents the Ballon d'Or trophy to the Three Lions' fans, having been crowned the world's best player last month.

Asked by reporters if Kane was England's greatest-ever player, Tuchel said: "I don't know, but he is up there, of course. It's now proven, and it's nice when things are proven in sports.

"He has his collection of prizes, he has his records, and he will build on these records, he will score more goals for us and get more games.

"Tomorrow, he will start for us, of course. He will start as the captain and it will be a big occasion, to present the Ballon d'Or trophy, to bring it to the country.

"And to have that embedded in the same day where he gets his all-time record… it will be a beautiful occasion."

“A beautiful, beautiful occasion.”  #ThreeLions skipper @HKane is set to make history at @wembleystadium  https://t.co/pqH91IidZ7

Kane has scored 13 goals for England in 2026, with only Kane himself in 2021 scoring more in a single calendar year for the Three Lions (16).

Four of those goals came as braces against Croatia (two in June, two in October) with no England player ever scoring multiple goals in three straight games against a single opponent.

Kane has also netted braces in his last two appearances for England overall (versus Croatia and Czechia), meaning he could become the first player since Wayne Rooney, in March 2009, to net two or more goals in three consecutive games for the Three Lions.

But Tuchel feels Kane's playmaking ability is what sets him apart from every other striker on the planet.

Asked if any other player could do what Kane does, Tuchel said: "Maybe not at the moment. Everyone plays differently.

"On the very highest level, Lionel Messi developed a completely new style of number nine at Barcelona and dropped everywhere.

"But he was more of a dribbler and accelerator from these spaces, Harry is more a passer and an accelerator through his passing range.

"Everyone is different. Harry is quite unique in the way he does it. That's not the only thing; he's also in and around the box, and you still want the ball to drop to him if it's a one or two-touch finish. He's the one who is clinical and finishes on the very highest level.

"That's why he got the biggest individual award in the game, because he's a unique player at the moment."

England only need a point against Croatia to secure their place in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could still top Group A3, with a trip to Spain to come on Sunday.

Danny Kelly, a prominent journalist across music and sport, has died, at the age of 69, after a battle with cancer.

Kelly, a lifelong Tottenham fan, announced in March on talkSPORT - where he had worked for almost two decades - that he had been diagnosed with oesophageal cancer.

A music lover, Kelly spent time a editor of NME and, later, Q magazine. He joined talkSPORT in late 2007, and went on to host a number of the radio station’s programmes.

Kelly was most recently heard as host of The Athletic’s award-winning Tottenham podcast ‘The View From The Lane’.

#1843. Who Manchester United stars 'want' to replace Michael Carrick - and it’s not Mauricio Pochettino

Michael Carrick has been pictured arriving at Carrington, potentially for the last time as Manchester United manager, before he is likely to be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, though reports claim that some players want Unai Emery.

It was business as usual for the under-fire Carrick on Wednesday morning as he arrived at Man Utd’s AON Complex in order to take training with the players who are not currently away on international duty.

However, it is expected that the decision to sack Carrick will be made later today some 800 miles away in Monaco, where chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are travelling to hold a meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls the sporting operation at the club.

It is understood that while no final decision has yet been made, Berrada and Wilcox are likely to recommend to Ratcliffe that a change is needed in an attempt to turn around United’s dismal run of form that has left them sitting in the Premier League relegation zone with one win from 10 games.

United’s majority owners the Glazers will also reportedly be part of that meeting, which is said to have been pre-planned and part of regular talks between the club hierarchy to discuss strategy. Ratcliffe has a home in Monaco, where his company INEOS also have offices.

It was widely reported on Wednesday morning that United were in the process of finalising a deal with Pochettino in the event that they part ways with Carrick, with personal terms close to being agreed.

Former Tottenham, Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain and Southampton boss Pochettino is currently the head coach of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and only signed a new contract through the 2030 World Cup back in August, after leading the USA to the World Cup last 16 on home soil in the summer.

However, there is a clause included in that deal that would allow United to release him from it early for a fee of $10million (£7.5m). The USA have a crucial two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti coming up, with the first game in Miami on Saturday.

Ex-Newcastle manager Eddie Howe had also been thought to be a favoured candidate to replace Carrick after reportedly turning down an approach from Crystal Palace, along with former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann.

Antonio Conte had also been linked with the post, along with Aston Villa’s Emery and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler.

talkSPORT claim that United’s senior stars expect Carrick to be sacked and Pochettino to become their new manager, marking his first return to the Premier League since an ill-fated one-season spell at Chelsea in 2023/24.

However, the same report says that some United players were hoping for the appointment of Emery, who is set to sign a new long-term contract extension at Villa Park instead.

#1842. ‘People pay for tickets to see Lamine’ – Czechia boss rues Yamal absence

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Czechia head coach Santi Denia admits he was disappointed to learn that Lamine Yamal will miss their meeting with Spain on Thursday, not least for fans who have bought tickets.

Denia will go up against the country of his birth in the Nations League, having previously coached Spain's under-18, under-21 and under-23 sides.

There is little riding on the game, given Czechia have lost their first four matches in Group A3 and cannot reach the quarter-finals, while La Roja's progression is already guaranteed.

And those in attendance at Slavia Prague's epet ARENA will not see Yamal, who is sidelined with a minor knee injury he sustained during Barcelona's victory over Atletico Madrid at the weekend.

Yamal's Barca team-mates Rodri and Dani Olmo are also out, and Denia would rather be going up against the world champions at full strength.

"We wanted Lamine to be there, but we don't control that. People pay for tickets to see Lamine," he said in an interview with Cadena Ser.

"We'll see what team Spain field and what team we can field. We have no injuries, and that's what's important."

In the 2026-27 edition of the Nations League, Yamal has scored four goals and supplied one assist in four outings – England captain and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is the only player to outscore him, with six goals.

Beautiful city. Beautiful kit.  Spain will be wearing white in Prague. 🇪🇸 #VamosEspaña | #NationsLeague https://t.co/ioEzKIkNDS

— Spanish Football (@SpainIsFootball) November 11, 2026

But Denia knows Spain have plenty of quality players waiting in the wings, adding: "Should I tell you the substitutes? That's why Spain are the best.

"It's a shame those players are not here, because people want to see them, but we're going to try to win the game and do things right.

"It doesn't change anything for us. Spain's structure is the same. To defend against Lamine, you need help, but you always have to do it as a team.

"You must defend and attack as a team. We don't ask the players to go into individual duels."

Spain have gone unbeaten in their last 42 matches since losing to Colombia in a friendly in March 2024, and they won the reverse fixture between the sides 3-1 last month.

#1841. 'Chosen one' or 'cooked'? Manchester United fans split on Mauricio Pochettino move

Social media is abuzz with reaction to the news that Mauricio Pochettino is likely to become the next Manchester United manager.

The Athletic reported on Wednesday that the Red Devils had made contact with the USA national team coach, with suggestions that personal terms are close to being finalised.

Under-fire current boss Michael Carrick remains in his post for now, taking training on Wednesday morning as United chiefs discuss their next steps forward in a meeting in Monaco.

Man Utd fans have been calling for change after their club’s worst-ever start to a Premier League season, which sees the Red Devils sit in the relegation zone after 10 games.

Some fans are confident that Pochettino’s arrival would spark a turnaround in fortunes, with one even going as far as to predict a return to “the glory days”.

Others were far more pessimistic. On X, a few United fans - and supporters of other clubs - posted memes suggesting that replacing Carrick with Pochettino was practically like-for-like, claiming that the Red Devils will not improve under their new coach.

One United fan took it one step further, claiming that Pochettino has “no tactics” and that his side are “cooked”.

In a similar vein, another fan shared her disappointment that the club were not looking to hire Antonio Conte.

Another commented that hiring Pochettino was a sign of how mediocrity had become accepted at Old Trafford.

One United supporter stated: “The only positive about getting Pochettino is he might get us relegated.”

However, certainly not every United fan is disappointed by the news. Chants for Pochettino have already been created, while one fan labelled the Argentine as “the chosen one”.

#1840. Brazilian Alysson becomes a starter after injury-hit first year at Villa

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 18:30

Alysson has taken advantage of Aston Villa’s rebuild to establish himself in unai Emery’s side, scoring in last Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger, who joined from Gremio in January, has overcome an injury-hit first six months to become a starter in the Premier League.

Aston Villa’s season has been defined by resilience. The team lost more than half of its starters in the last transfer window, but Emery, with many signings, has reinvented his group again. They went seven games unbeaten before the current run of four without a win. Part of that change has come from a Brazilian who was already there: Alysson.

Signed in January from Gremio at the age of 19, he suffered in the first half of the year. Three different injuries kept him out of 18 games, according to Transfermarkt. As a result, he only played three games for Villa, coming off the bench against Brighton and Hove Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers (both in February) and Chelsea (March).

‘He spent more time injured than available to train and play,’ Emery admitted last month about the player’s previous season.

With a full pre-season, the Brazilian was able to change his status and string games together. On Sunday, he scored one of the goals in the 4-4 draw with United, in a standout performance. It is an unlikely story given the right winger’s age and the pressure of the Premier League, where Gustavo Nunes, a former Gremio team-mate of Alysson, has still not made a start for Brentford, the club he has played for since August 2024.

More reliable physically, thanks to a full pre-season, the youngster was able to be available more often and take advantage of the overhaul in Villa’s attack following the departures of Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins and Leon Bailey. In his first months he was compared to the Jamaican winger.

‘He has more or less similar characteristics or qualities to Bailey: he is left-footed and plays on the right,’ Emery said in February. ‘And he has huge potential.’

In the first game of 2026-27, he showed he would have more time on the pitch, playing 17 minutes in the defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup. He then came off the bench in the next eight games, with a short break for a muscle problem in September, and his performances earned him a starting place.

Introduced at half-time in the defeat to Nottingham Forest, he arrived in the box to head in and level the score. Against Fenerbahce, he produced a good individual move on the wing, went past a defender into the area and passed for Tammy Abraham to tap in. Those displays earned him starts against Newcastle United, Viking, Manchester City, Fulham and, finally, Manchester United. Against Viking, he had a standout match for his ability to dribble and win duels, and directly caused an own goal.

At Old Trafford, he did everything but make it rain. He opened the scoring with a first-time shot through goalkeeper Senne Lammens’ legs, forced the Belgian’s rebound for Nicolas Jackson’s goal, and won the penalty converted by McGinn when he went at Diogo Dalot and was brought down. He could also have scored again, but a chip over Lammens went wide.

‘Alysson is understanding things well and is giving us what I want,’ Emery said in September.

‘Every minute he is playing, practising, he is fantastic,’ Emery added in October. ‘We can see his power. We can see that if he can get consistency, a lot of things he is doing: “Wow!”’

The numbers illustrate his role. Villa have been much more vertical this season thanks to the speed of Jackson, Johan Manzambi, George Hemmings and, of course, Alysson. The Brazilian ranks second of all players in the Premier League for sprints, with 22.7, and reached 35.4km/h in one match, the highest by a Villa player and the eighth-highest in the league, according to Sofascore. In the Champions League, despite only one start and 127 minutes across four games, he is among the leaders for successful dribbles (nine, 11th in the competition level with Jackson) and ground duels won (16).

‘Alysson was incredible,’ said Villa midfielder Emiliano Buendia after the 3-1 win over Viking. ‘He is showing all his potential and his ability to play on the wings.’

Because of his age, being in his first year in a new country and the injury history, Emery is cautious with the Brazilian. In different interviews, the Spanish manager has praised the youngster while stressing he still has a lot to learn, especially tactically.

‘He should be a player who can help us. So we need to be patient, seek consistency and be careful with him every day,’ he said on 19 October. ‘This season, he has felt some pain and we need to try to be careful, but also give him confidence so he is comfortable.’

‘Alysson is improving his consistency because he has very good individual qualities, but he also needs to understand the importance of consistency in the collective aspect: defending, attacking, positioning and understanding combinations with team-mates,’ he explained two days later.

Emery remains an admirer and sees the right winger as a possible Brazil international. ‘My expectation is that Alysson can also get there,’ he said after the call-up of Villa team-mate Joao Gomes. At 20, the forward has shown on the pitch what he can do, and if he becomes more consistent, it is only a matter of time before he is called up.

#1839. ST MIRREN 0 RANGERS 2: It's back to the grind for McInnes' men as they show grit to see off Buddies

By KEVIN MCKENNA AT MARBILL COACHES STADIUM

Published: 17:42 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:51 EST, 7 November 2026

At some stage, you would suspect Rangers are going to find their groove under Derek McInnes.

But until then, they will happily settle for just getting points on the board. How they go about it doesn’t really matter in the grand scheme of things.

This hard-fought victory in Paisley — much like so many of Rangers’ Premiership wins this season — was all about substance over style.

Yes, there were flashes of quality here and there. But it was more to do with doing the ugly stuff well than anything else. Fortunately for McInnes, his side are proving to be adept at doing so.

It’s a handy habit to have at their disposal. We saw it in recent draws at Dundee and Hearts last month, managing to come away with something when they probably deserved nothing.

With nobody knowing what version of Celtic are going to turn up on any given week, all Rangers can do is stay within touching distance of the league leaders — a point in front ahead of their meeting with Kilmarnock this afternoon — until they come to blows again in the new year.

Rangers skipper Neil nets with the aid of a deflection to put his side two goals up

Rangers wasted no time getting themselves on the front foot. St Mirren barely got a kick in the opening exchanges, and on the odd occasion they did, possession was turned over far too easily.

Badredine Bouanani had the visitors’ first effort of the night on six minutes, cutting inside from the right flank before pulling the trigger from 20 yards, but it lacked the power to properly test Jacob Chapman in the Saints goal.

The keeper had to be far more alert five minutes later, pulling off a wonderful reaction stop to deny Ryan Naderi finishing off Kevin Kelsy’s headed knockdown. You would have put your house on the in-form Czech finding the net.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed over from the resulting corner.

Having finally settled down, St Mirren gave their opponents a perfect opportunity to take the lead, when Samuel Ramos brought down James Penrice on the angle of the Buddies’ box.

There didn’t appear to be a great deal of contact, but it didn’t take long for VAR to confirm referee Nick Walsh’s decision.

Naderi stepped up to do what he failed to do moments earlier, coolly slotting into the bottom corner to register his ninth goal in all competitions this season.

From looking as if he was likely to be on his way out of Ibrox over the summer, the 23-year-old has become one of the first names on McInnes’ team sheet.

Penrice goes down under Ramos' challenge to earn Rangers a penalty in the first half

And perhaps the most exciting thing from a Rangers perspective is that he is still a million miles from being the finished article. But playing with this sort of confidence, he’s only going to get better.

He was involved in a lovely free-flowing counter shortly after the half-hour mark, with the ball eventually falling to Kim Min-su on the penalty spot. However, the South Korean delayed getting his shot off and the chance was gone.

When running full-flight at defences, the 20-year-old is a delight to watch in that No10 role.

There isn’t anyone in the country better at finding pockets of space between the lines and taking the ball on the turn. But for all that there is to enjoy about his game, his decision-making in the key moments undoubtedly needs work.

A woeful ball out from Olwethu Makhanya set up a two-v-two for the hosts before the break, with Ramos drilling straight at Ivor Pandur from inside the area. With the whole goal to aim at, the Spaniard should have done much better.

The same goes for Jake Young, who blasted high and wide from a promising position a minute later.

Naderi is hailed by Min-su after putting the visitors ahead from the spot

As dominant as Rangers were, you never got the feeling their lead was particularly secure, such is their tendency to play themselves into trouble every now and then.

Fernandez is the worst culprit for it. Fortunately for him, his recovery pace gets him out of jail more often than not. He needed it on a couple of occasions here.

A delightful threaded ball from Bouanani found the feet of Min-su inside the box on 47 minutes but under heavy pressure, he was unable to prod beyond Chapman who’d rushed off his line to meet him. It was hard to be too critical of the Rangers midfielder this time.

Chapman was once again called into action to thwart Kelsy from close range after the Venezuelan escaped the clutches of his marker to collect Min-su’s pass in behind.

He then skewed an effort wide at the back post from an excellent Nico Raskin delivery from the right. It was a night on which very little came off for the big man in front of goal.

To his credit, he kept plugging away, and played a key role in Rangers’ doubling their advantage just after the hour mark, with his driving run causing a bit of chaos in the Buddies backline, before captain Dan Neil swept a loose ball into the bottom corner via the aid of a big deflection to give Chapman absolutely no chance of saving.

With his first touch, substitute Eseosa Sule wasted a glorious chance to reduce the deficit after being left all alone at the back post to stab home Declan John’s cross.

With the ball seemingly destined for the back of the net, Rangers keeper Pandur produced a stunning save on the stretch to turn the ball round the post.

The Croatian’s signing went somewhat under the radar over the summer, but he has demonstrated time and time again that he is a man for the big occasion. He’ll win this side plenty of points between now and the end of the season.

McInnes applauds the away support after signing off for the international break with a win

St Mirren came into this one having won just once in their past eight, but you wouldn’t have guessed they were struggling for confidence given the way in which they threw everything at the game in an effort to get a result.

It wasn’t for lack of trying, with Luke Thomas testing Pandur from range before Calvin Ramsay’s follow-up header clipped the post.

That would be as close as Saints would come, as Rangers dug in to grind out an ugly — but ultimately deserved — win on the road.

They will need to be far better, far more consistently if they want to get their hands on the Premiership title come May. But that’s a worry for another day.

#1838. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Cisse and Pulisic score in hard-fought victory

AC Milan secured a much-needed three points on Sunday afternoon as they beat an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.

The groundwork for the victory was laid in the first half, when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

It means that a top four spot has been reclaimed for the time being while waiting to see how the game between Inter and Como plays out, and it eases some of the pressure heading into the international break.

Ruben Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa started on the front foot and they immediately created an opening inside the first minute. Koni De Winter allowed Osmajic to run off his shoulder and get a shot off from the left side of the box, but Maignan watched it roll narrowly wide of the far post.

One minute after Vitinha had back-heeled a near-post cross into Maignan’s hands, Milan created their first opening. Pulisic’s cross from the byline wasn’t well-aimed but the clearance fell straight to Ramos, who didn’t quite connect right with his effort and sent it a couple of yards wide of the far post.

Milan continued to knock on the door and Ramos almost found himself on the end of a golden opportunity when Gila was found on the overlap and provided a cut-back, though Marcandalli did brilliantly to cut out the danger.

Then, in the 13th minute, Milan did take the lead through Alphadjo Cisse. The goal was assisted by Adrien Rabiot who found the run of the Italian with a nice square ball, but Pulisic was the one who won possession back on the high press to create the opportunity, which was well finished by Cisse for his eighth goal of the campaign.

In the 19th minute, the Rossoneri doubled their lead. Another successful press forced Ostigard into a mistake as his square ball back towards the goalkeeper was cut off by Ramos. The Portuguese squared to Pulisic after evading a defender, and the American made no mistake as he fired inside the near post to make it 2-0.

Right on the half-hour mark, Genoa thought they had got themselves back into the game when Osmajic headed past Maignan having escaped his man to be found by Vitinha’s flick-on. However, the offside flag was raised and the decision was upheld, though it looked very close.

Despite being two goals up, Milan never gave the impression of being in control and Genoa had a couple of half-chances towards the end of the half, including an Ostigard header that Maignan managed to claim.

The start to the second half was certainly a fractious one, and the Milan players were surrounding the referee Davide Massa five minutes into it when Rabiot seized on a loose touch from Marcandalli to run in behind.

He was dragged back by the defender who appeared to be the last man, but a yellow card was deemed to be sufficient. Rabiot got a yellow too for his protests, and three members of the Milan coaching staff were shown a red.

Amorim opted to make a couple of changes on the hour mark, with Cisse making way for Omari Hutchinson and Diawara coming off for Filippo Terracciano.

As the game entered the final 20 minutes, Milan began to look comfortable with their lead but at times complacent too. Musah gave possession away in the left-back position and it gave Vitinha a dangerous position to get a shot off, though Maignan did well to parry it away.

The pressure continued to come from the Rossoblu, and El Shaarawy had a chance off the bench when a cross found him in the box. He brought it down well, but Terracciano got a knee to it to deflect it over. Pulisic made way for Ardon Jashari after.

Inside the final few minutes Pervis Estupinan became the last player to come, replacing Musah. The sub was made just before El Shaarawy lined up a free-kick from about 22 yards out, and it would yield Genoa’s route back into the game.

The initial shot was blocked as it went into a crowd but was not cleared, allowing Ellertsson all the time in the world to step up and strike one from distance that nestled inside the right post with Maignan rooted. Game on with two minutes of normal time left.

#1837. England XI vs Croatia: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Nations League

Dan Burn and James Hill have been added to the England squad as replacements for Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa ahead of Thursday’s match against Croatia.

The Three Lions face Croatia at Wembley Stadium in their penultimate Nations League group game, before completing their group-phase in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday.

Manchester City centre-back Guehi was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with a hip injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest but has now pulled out of the squad.

In his place, Thomas Tuchel called up the 34-year-old Newcastle defender. He had said on Friday that “difficult phone calls” had been had with Burn, Dean Henderson and Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson when leaving them behind. But the former is now in as Guehi’s replacement.

Meanwhile, it was announced on Tuesday morning that Konsa will not be available for the Croatia game, but is expected to return to full training later in the week ahead of the Spain fixture. He has already joined up with England and was following his own individualised training programme while the rest of the squad trained at Tottenham on Wednesday afternoon.

The other omission from training on Wednesday was Inter Milan’s Djed Spence, is now a doubt for the Croatia match. Spence, despite being right-footed, is in the squad as a left-back.

As such, Tuchel must decide whether to hand Hill a senior debut or reshuffle his defence with Ben White coming in at right-back, thus allowing Jarell Quansah to partner Burn in the middle.

Captain Harry Kane is expected to start and will overtake Peter Shilton to become England’s all-time most-capped player.

Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka (injury) and Noni Madueke (selection decision) are not in the squad this month but the head coach has explained that he sees his options on the right wing as being Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha, Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White and Fulham’s Josh King.

#1836. Kevin De Bruyne: Premier League club ‘assessing real chances’ of signing Man City legend from Napoli

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 18:58, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 19:01

One Premier League club are reportedly considering a shock move for Napoli and Belgium playmaker Kevin De Bruyne in January.

The 35-year-old spent 10 glorious years at Manchester City and earned legendary status at the Etihad Stadium where he won 19 trophies and made 422 appearances, scoring 108 goals and registering 177 assists.

City decided not to extend De Bruyne’s contract at the end of the 2024-25 season and he subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football.

De Bruyne’s debut campaign with Napoli was stuck by injury and he was limited to only 16 starts across all competitions, but he has since played in all 15 games across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists.

The playmaker’s current contract is due to expire in June 2027, but it has been suggested that he could leave Napoli sooner than expected.

Last month, former Napoli striker Roberto Carlos Sosa stated that the “spark never really ignited” between De Bruyne and the Naples outfit.

Italian news outlet Calciomercato have since reported that De Bruyne is going through a ‘mental decline’ and the midfielder make look to pursue a sensational return to the Premier League in January.

The report adds that Everton would be interested in signing De Bruyne and have already initiated ‘first contacts’ with the player’s representatives to understand their ‘real chances’ of signing him.

In order for the transfer to materialise, Napoli would need to be convinced to sanction De Bruyne’s exit midway through the season, and it remains unknown as to whether they would demand a fee for a player with six months remaining on his contract.

De Bruyne is widely regarded as one of the best midfielders in Premier League history and thrived as an advanced playmaker at Man City behind the central striker.

He was also capable of operating as a false nine or in a deep-lying midfield role, dictating play from just in front of the back four, while he also has experience out on the right and left flanks, though he does not possess the acceleration he once had.

At Everton, De Bruyne could be a contender to play in a deeper midfield position alongside James Garner and/or Harrison Armstrong, who have featured regularly under David Moyes.

De Bruyne could also play further forward as a No.10, but this is where Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall has established himself as a key first-team figure with the Toffees.

Alternatively, the Belgian could rivals Brennan Johnson, Tyler Dibling and Merlin Rohl for starts on the right side of midfield.

Regardless of which position De Bruyne would play under Moyes, the midfielder would want assurances of regular first-team football before agreeing to join Everton or any other club should he leave Napoli.

#1835. Kane, Palmer and Paz: Mauricio Pochettino’s dream Manchester United XI revealed

Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly gearing up to become the new Manchester United manager, as club chiefs meet in Monaco to discuss Michael Carrick’s future.

A new face in the dugout is needed with the club currently languishing in the relegation zone after the worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Pochettino will be expected to be backed in the transfer window, both in January and moving forward, as Man Utd bid to get back to their glorious days of the past.

That would mean yet more serious investment in the squad, but what exactly would a Pochettino dream XI look like at United?

Senne Lammens may have thrown a few into his own net recently, but he is still a good goalkeeper and a relatively recent recruit. If it ain’t (totally) broke, don’t fix it.

Full-back has become a real problem for Man Utd. Luke Shaw’s poor injury record continues to affect both his fitness and form, and Diogo Dalot is clearly not up to the task despite being in his ninth season at Old Trafford.

At Tottenham particularly, Pochettino worked wonders with impressive and robust young full-backs, who grew into the league’s best under his tutelage. That brings Lewis Hall - even with a new contract - and Spurs’s Archie Gray into view.

Whether they would join Man Utd is another matter, but working with Pochettino would surely be an attractive pull. Hall and Gray have years ahead of them, but are also assured Premier League performers who are well-balanced between attack and defence. And in Gray, there are burgeoning leadership skills, too.

At centre-back, you could just imagine the Argentina connection bringing Lisandro Martinez back into scope for Man Utd’s medium-term future, and Pochettino has always relished the challenge of working with high-ceiling young players. Leny Yoro, still only 20, is certainly that.

Central midfield would be a mix of youth and experience, with Youri Tielemans taking the lead and Kobbie Mainoo learning alongside him. Meanwhile, a reunion with Chelsea’s Cole Palmer — who played by far his best football in blue during Pochettino’s tenure — would be a mouthwatering prospect.

But Palmer would be asked to play on the right, to make way for Bruno Fernandes’s replacement in attacking midfield. Quite conceivable is that the player in question would be Como’s Nico Paz, an Argentina international and the sort of promising No10 that Pochettino would love to work with and challenge to reach that next level.

#1834. Prediction: Serbia vs Germany

Germany face an important UEFA Nations League clash on Friday evening when they travel to Serbia in their penultimate Group A2 fixture.

Jurgen Klopp’s side currently sit third in the group and trail both the Netherlands and Greece by three points, meaning anything less than victory could severely damage their chances of reaching the quarter-finals. Serbia, meanwhile, have endured a miserable campaign and are already out of contention for a top-two finish.

Serbia’s Nations League campaign has been one to forget.

Veljko Paunovic’s side have lost all four of their matches in Group A2, beginning with a 2-1 home defeat to Greece before suffering losses against the Netherlands, Germany and the Dutch again in their most recent outing.

The Eagles have now lost six consecutive matches in all competitions and have managed only one victory since the end of 2025. As a result, they sit bottom of the group without a single point and can no longer qualify for the knockout stage.

While a top-two finish is impossible, Serbia can still avoid finishing last if they defeat Germany and produce a strong result in their final fixture.

There is additional bad news for the visitors, with midfielders Sasa Lukic and Nemanja Maksimovic suspended. Their absence places more responsibility on Sergej Milinkovic-Savic to control the midfield.

Up front, experienced striker Aleksandar Mitrovic is expected to earn his 107th international cap and should again be partnered by Mihajlo Cvetkovic.

Klopp’s team have won just one of their four group matches, drawing twice and losing once. After opening with a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands, Germany suffered a disappointing 1-0 home defeat to Greece before beating Serbia 2-0 at the Allianz Arena in Munich.

Their most recent fixture ended in a frustrating goalless draw against Greece, leaving them three points behind the top two heading into the final two matchdays.

The equation is simple: Germany need six points from matches against Serbia and the Netherlands if they are to give themselves the best possible chance of reaching the quarter-finals.

Klopp can at least call upon plenty of attacking talent. Kai Havertz is expected to lead the line once again, while Florian Wirtz should feature prominently. Exciting young players Said El Mala and Lennart Karl are also pushing for starting roles.

Marc-Andre ter Stegen remains Germany’s first-choice goalkeeper, while defenders Philipp Treu, Malick Thiaw and Yann Bisseck must be careful, as all three are one booking away from suspension.

Germany have not been particularly convincing throughout this Nations League campaign, but this fixture provides a clear opportunity to get their qualification hopes back on track.

Serbia have struggled badly for form, confidence and consistency, while suspensions further weaken an already fragile squad. Even if Klopp’s side are not at their very best, they should possess too much quality across the pitch. Even finding the back of the opposition net once is likely to prove a task too hard for the hosts.

#1833. Sir Jim Ratcliffe should be ashamed at how he is running Manchester United and treating Michael Carrick

“Best in class”? You’ve got to be joking, Jim. INEOS’s running of Man Utd has been a calamitous mess

As the latest Manchester United embarrassment meanders towards an inevitable conclusion, Sir Jim Ratcliffe can comfort himself in the knowledge that he has got some things right.

In an interview with BBC Sport last year, Ratcliffe admitted: “I recognise I’m unpopular at the moment. I’m prepared to be and can deal with being unpopular for a period of time.”

So far, so good. When you run a football club as badly as INEOS have done, thick skin is essential.

“Manchester United has come off the rails and we need to get it back on the rails,” Ratcliffe continued. Again, all correct for now.

“I believe that what we’re doing will put it back on the rails and we’ll finish up being where Liverpool or Real Madrid are today.”

For all this shambolic process has been entirely in keeping with how the club’s hierarchy operate, it is a shameful way to treat Carrick

Try not to laugh. Fast forward a year and United are spending the November international break in the relegation zone. It is their lowest position in the league after ten matches for 40 years.

It was INEOS who put forward Mission 21, the plan to deliver United a 21st league title by 2028 to mark the club’s 150th anniversary. Would winning the Championship count?

United fans need not worry, though. The good news is that the club is in safe hands. In 2024, Ratcliffe declared: “We need to populate all the key roles with people who are best in class. 10-out-of-10s.”

Step forward Omar Berrada, chief executive, and director of football Jason Wilcox. The brains trust are in Monaco for a meeting with Ratcliffe on Wednesday to discuss the club’s strategy and more specifically the future of Michael Carrick.

Except we already know the outcome because it leaked two days earlier. Berrada and Wilcox will recommend that Carrick is sacked as United embark on a mid-season manager search for the third year in a row.

For all this shambolic process has been entirely in keeping with how the club’s hierarchy operate, it is a shameful way to treat Carrick.

Sacking him is not the wrong decision. United have one league win all season and are a dream to play against. The squad is not good enough but results have still been abysmal under Carrick, who has showed no sign of turning things around.

However, that does not excuse how the situation has been handled. The 45-year-old made 464 appearances for the club. He won five Premier League titles at Old Trafford. While the fans have rightly aimed their fury at the players and the board in recent weeks, Carrick has retained their support.

And yet the incompetence of United’s leadership meant that he spent Tuesday at the club’s training ground, pretending it was business as usual despite knowing he would imminently be sacked.

The delay is said to be because Wilcox and Berrada want to inform Carrick face-to-face, but only after they consulted with Ratcliffe. That, of course, can only be done in person in Monaco and after waiting a couple of days for good measure. Add video calls to the list of things beyond this trio.

It is a laughable attempt at claiming to do things the right way, with the sacking decision effectively having already been made public.

This is a rudderless ship with no hope of success under the current leadership

To undermine that stance further, United are in talks with Mauricio Pochettino. Discussions are believed to be in the final stages and an agreement is close. All while Carrick remains in charge and shuffles papers at the training ground.

Nor is it any great surprise. Ratcliffe oversaw the Erik ten Hag debacle in 2024, when the club were set to sack the Dutchman and spoke to several replacements, only to then panic and give him a contract extension. Ten Hag was sacked a few months later.

Dan Ashworth stuck his head in for five months to the cost of £4.1million. It took 16 months to work out Sir Dave Brailsford knew nothing about football. Wilcox was involved in the appointment of back-three zealot Ruben Amorim and then forcefully suggested to the manager he might want to not play a back-three. Amorim was gone days later.

Back to Ratcliffe and his prophetic words. “They made a complete cock-up of it, shocking really,” he told The Times last year, when asked about the club’s previous leadership under the Glazers.

“The first management group, they thought they understood and wanted to get involved in buying footballers but they didn’t have the knowledge to buy footballers. They went in the marketplace, spraying money around and it was just random, wasn’t it?”

Fortunately Ratcliffe had the “best in class” to correct that. Wilcox oversaw the summer window and had the clever plan of caring about only one position. No more randomness. This squad would be rebuilt in instalments, starting in midfield.

Forget that the defence was in dire need of reinforcements. Or that the midfield overhaul did not involve signing an elite midfielder. Or that no serious club has ever operated in that way.

That was the support Carrick was given, having led United back into the Champions League. Hopefully Pochettino will have his say in the defenders that arrive next summer. Perhaps the next manager after him will be allowed a forward signing or two.

It is absurd that Wilcox will come away from the Monaco summit with another manager gone and his job still intact. But then Ratcliffe has backed himself into a corner, having stuck with Wilcox through all the mistakes of the past two years.

Sack Wilcox and admit a failure of leadership in putting the wrong man in place? Or keep Wilcox and in doing so admit the “best in class” soundbite was just that, confirming this is a rudderless ship with no hope of success under the current leadership?

For now, it will be the easy decision. Remove another manager and start the cycle again. From Ratcliffe at the top to Wilcox and Berrada below him, all the way down to the players on the pitch, United have individuals out of their depth at every level.

Carrick has clearly not delivered this season either but the disrespect in the final hours of his reign is further evidence that he is better off out of this mess.

#1832. Rangers boss Derek McInnes piles the praise on in-form striker Ryan Naderi

Published: 18:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 18:59 EST, 7 November 2026

Rangers manager Derek McInnes heaped praise on Ryan Naderi after the Czech added another goal to his tally in the 2-0 win over St Mirren – but insisted there is still far more to come from his in-form striker.

The 23-year-old stepped up to slot home a first-half penalty to take his total to nine for the season in all competitions, with skipper Dan Neil adding a second shortly after the hour-mark to seal a valuable three points on the road.

The result moves McInnes’ men to within a point of Premiership leaders Celtic – who take on Kilmarnock this afternoon – ahead of the international break.

And the manager was delighted with the way in which his frontman shrugged off an earlier miss to take responsibility for the spot-kick which set Rangers on their way in what was a potential banana-skin encounter in Paisley.

‘His first port of call is to make sure he’s a handful to play against and I thought he was that,’ said McInnes. ‘I thought he ran the gaps, he made sure every one of their centre-backs knew he was there, which is very important.

‘He needs to build that reputation for being horrible to play against, but equally at a club like Rangers you’re going to get judged on the goals.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes (pictured) is thrilled with Ryan Naderi's performances

The Czech striker (left) celebrates with Kim Min-su after breaking the deadlock in Paisley

‘If you’re going to lead the line for us, then getting those goals is so important and thankfully with his stats he’s really contributing.

‘He’s probably a bit annoyed he never added to it, but I thought he was terrific.

‘You can’t be unsure, you can’t be thinking, “Do I belong here?”.

‘I think he’s totally shown that he’s somebody you can depend on, somebody that can be trusted, somebody that you can rely on to get goals as well as bring in good performances.’

Rangers are now unbeaten in their last 12, but although McInnes is pleased with his side’s progress after a sticky start to the season, he is under no illusions that there is much to improve on.

‘That type of form gets you close to where you want to get to,’ he said. ‘There’s still loads of work to do and loads of improvements in the team, as you can see.

‘If we take our chances, we take the game away from St Mirren and while it’s still 1-0, they are always going to keep going.

‘I still think that if we can win games and keep improving as we go along, then that’s the nature of the job for us. It’s just all about winning here.

‘The form has been really good, but we’re conscious that we’re not home and dry. We’re not the real deal yet. We’ve got loads of work to do to maintain that.

Dan Neil scored the second goal just after the hour-mark to put the game beyond St Mirren

‘Every game we’ve won has been hard-fought and we’ve had to play well to get the win.’

Saints boss Craig McLeish wasn’t happy with referee Nick Walsh’s decision to award the visitors a first-half penalty after James Penrice went down under the challenge of Samuel Ramos.

‘If that’s the criteria for contact in the box, then fine,’ he said.

‘But Kabs [Ismael Kabia] gets wiped out in the second half after he puts a cross in. I don’t even know if anyone looks at it.

‘I get that if the ref gives it on the field, then it’s maybe difficult for VAR to overturn it.

‘I think if he doesn’t give it there and then, I don’t think VAR gets involved to give it.

‘It’s a difficult one and it’s a frustrating one from our point of view, but there’s also bits leading up to it getting to that situation that we need to deal with better.

‘I need to be careful with what I’m saying.

‘Somebody just told me that there, it’s like our seventh penalty we’ve given away in 13 games, which from our point of view is not good enough. We can’t give teams goals and put ourselves in a hole like that.’

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 19:11

Manchester co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe still has confidence in director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, the latest report has claimed.

The future of several figures at Old Trafford have been questioned in recent weeks given the club find themselves 18th in the Premier League table.

Head coach Michael Carrick appears likely to lose his job after Wednesday, when senior leaders of Ratcliffe's INEOS group are set to meet to discuss the manager's future.

It is impossible for fans to know the true extent of their roles at Old Trafford, but the fact that United have repeatedly failed in the transfer market is a damning indictment of their time at the club.

The Red Devils focused on their attack in the summer of 2025, only for the likes of Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko to disappoint, and there is still no clear left-winger in the squad other than Marcus Rashford.

United signed three midfielders in the summer of 2026, but there are serious question marks about Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Carlos Baleba has struggled with injuries.

Carrick will almost certainly be relived of his coaching duties, and while results and performances suggest that it would be the right call, he has been routinely let down by those above him.

Responsibility for United's struggles must ultimately fall on Ratcliffe, especially as Carrick is set to be the third boss sacked since he took control of sporting operations in 2024.
