#1830. Player Ratings: Genoa 1-2 AC Milan – De Winter, Pulisic and Rabiot take charge

AC Milan responded to the criticism with an important win at Genoa on Sunday afternoon. A few players made the difference and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After the mid-week failure against Ferencvaros, Milan knew that three points were more or less a must against Genoa. Thankfully, aside from a dramatic ending, it was a comfortable game for the Rossoneri and a few of the players also got to send some strong signals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

👎 Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

👔 Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

Maignan (6.5): We saw a couple of good stops from him, including one on Vitinha in the second half, and his distribution was decent. He couldn’t really do anything about the goal either, as it was a really good effort from Ellertsson.

Gila (6): I liked his performance overall but there were a couple of moments that dragged down the rating for me, more specifically the fouls he committed. Put simply, he was a bit too rash and it was after one of the free-kicks he caused that Genoa scored their goal.

De Winter (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Diawara (6): He was carded for a very rash challenge, but apart from that, he kept his calm at the back and had decent positioning throughout. It’s not like Genoa threatened Milan a lot, but enough for a pass here still.

Moreira (6.5): It was a lively start from him, I would say, with some good moments on that right flank. However, the end product wasn’t always amazing (some blocked shots), and he faded a bit attacking-wise as the game went on. Solid though and he did put in a defensive shift at the end.

Modric (7): We got to see some really nice flicks and quick play from him today. Defensively, he contributed as well, which was especially clear with a last-ditch toe-poke to avoid a 1v1 for Genoa. There was one poor pass into the middle which could have proved costly, but the rest was good.

Rabiot (7.5): He was back to his usual self today after what was a subpar display against Ferencvaros. Great movement between the lines and elegance on the ball were his main strengths, also getting the assist for the opener.

Musah (6): We have to praise him for doing well in a ‘new’ position, following the instructions from Amorim nearly perfectly. What stopped him from getting a higher rating here was the big giveaway at the end, which Genoa really should have done more with.

Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

Cisse (7): It was a very tidy finish to give Milan the lead, showing once again that he knows how to turn up in the right place at the right time. However, for a higher rating, I would have liked to see more in his 1v1s, which weren’t always so successful.

Ramos (5.5): I’m torn here. It was unselfish to pass to Pulisic for the second goal rather than shooting himself, so that deserves praise. However, I actually think he was very sloppy in open play with heavy touches and positioning that sometimes left a lot to be desired. I suppose the big question is how much his defensive work rate is worth to the rating.

Terracciano (6): Surprisingly good! He had a crucial deflection on a shot from El Shaarawy and also headed the ball away quite a few times in the end, certainly contributing to the three points.

Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

Jashari (6): We didn’t see much in terms of attacking contributions and build-up, since he came on with ten minutes to go, but he was responsible for a few clearances at the end.

Estupinan (5.5): I don’t think it was much of a foul, but in those moments, you shouldn’t even give the referee the opportunity to blow the whistle. He knows that.

Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

I thought this is also a tale of 2 flanks, the right flank with Pulišić and Moreira & sometimes Gila stepping up was terrific while the left flank with Musah, Cissé é Diwarara looked a bit dodgy offensively. I don’t know what to think of this formula overall, but knowing Amorim, I won’t surprised if he tries yet another tactic with Ramos as an AM, Gila as a midfielder,… with him you can’t be sure. Maignan: Overall he was there when needed, and I don’t think he can be blamed for that shot from way out. Musah: I almost pity the guy. He started looking a bit decent in the midfield, then Amorim throws him as a RB for one game, then as a LB in the next. But I think it mostly shows how little confidence Amorim has in Bartesaghi & Estupiñán, which to be fair, is understandable. / Estupiñán: came in late and caused a foul that almost gave away a draw, such an Estupiñán thing to do… Diawara: Still a bit raw and rough around the edges, but overall I did like his efforts. Terracciano: we actually survived having him, Musah as LB then Estupiñán on the pitch… he wasn’t so bad this time apart from a horrible pass. Which makes me thing maybe against Bologna, we should REALLY have subbed him in instead of having Musah on the flank and weakening the midfield… but the past is the past. De Winter: I wasn’t actually super impressed by him. Almost gave away a goal one minute in and managed to make Vitinha look like Vitinha sometimes, but then again considering how much Gila steps up, I guess he can be a bit overloaded. Gila: I don’t like him leaving too much gap behind, but honestly his attacks look more polished than Pavlović’s. Moreira: not that good defensively, but offensively, my man is a demon. Modrić: Honestly, I think the recent adjustments of Amorim (or whatever one can call them), suit him a bit better. He looked more rejuvinated recently. Rabiot: some check if he has a knife, because he was tearing through Genoa’s midfield like butter. Cissé: his speed is a liability for sure, but this kid sure knows how to make himself available. Pulišić: his best game in a while IMO, he scored, pressed like there is no tomorrow, helped in the defense, won duels,… Ramos: the simple fact that in that position in that moment, he chose to set up Pulišić instead of trying to score himself from what was already a closed angle, is a positive. Overall, we’re 5 points from first place, which ain’t bad and I’m assuming inter is going to tear through Como as usual so we might be fourth. Let’s now hope the dreaded international break won’t claim any more victims from our side…

#1829. How Thomas Frank could raid Tottenham in Crystal Palace transfer spree

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Thomas Frank is the frontrunner to take over from Pierre Sage as Crystal Palace manager.

The Dane has been out of work since stepping away from football following his departure from Tottenham in February.

Frank was on Palace’s shortlist over the summer as they looked for a replacement for Oliver Glasner, but they instead opted to bring in Sage following a successful spell with Ligue 1 side Lens.

Just 10 games into the new season, though, Sage is expected to leave Palace with the club rock bottom of the Premier League table heading into the international break.

A succession plan is already under way, with Frank at the top of a long list of potential candidates to take over at Selhurst Park.

Despite a disastrous eight-month period at Spurs - leaving the club sitting just above the relegation zone - Frank is still well regarded from his time at Brentford and is viewed as an experienced Premier League operator.

Should Frank take charge at Palace, he will likely need reinforcements in January and could look to raid his former club to steer the Eagles away from the relegation zone.

With that in mind, Standard Sport has identified three Spurs players Palace could look at if Frank takes the reins.

Brought in from Atletico Madrid last January as Frank desperately looked to bolster his midfield options after Rodrigo Bentancur underwent hamstring surgery, Gallagher’s return to the Premier League has not gone quite as well as he would have hoped.

The former Chelsea man chose Spurs over Aston Villa not only because of a desire to return to London and a healthy wage packet but also to put himself in contention for England’s World Cup squad.

Instead, the midfielder became embroiled in a messy relegation battle and was, for a period, a lightning rod for criticism due to his limited capabilities in possession.

Gallagher played an important role for Roberto De Zerbi towards the end of last season but has seen his minutes limited this term following the arrivals of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

A return to Palace, where he enjoyed arguably his most productive season as a professional on loan from Chelsea in 2021/22, would make sense for both parties.

Spurs, though, are said to be reluctant to part ways with the 26-year-old.

Another player Spurs would ideally want to keep hold of is centre-back Marcos Senesi, who only joined the club in the summer on a free transfer from Bournemouth.

De Zerbi was keen to bring Senesi to north London because of his ability to play out from the back, but the Argentine has so far seen his minutes restricted with Dutch duo Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke Spurs’ first-choice centre-back pairing.

Senesi is a good tactical fit and provides important cover for Spurs, but his desire to play regularly could be tested if Palace come in with an offer when the January window opens.

Palace have not suitably replaced Maxence Lacroix or Marc Guehi, so a new centre-back would likely be a priority for Frank, who instigated Spurs’ initial interest in Senesi.

Spurs’ top goalscorer last season has been banished from the first team after failing to force a move away from the club over the summer.

The Brazilian has been training with the Under-21s and played and scored in their 2-2 EFL Trophy draw against Cheltenham last month.

Spurs will be desperate to sanction a move for Richarlison in January, and while a return to Brazil has been mooted, Palace could provide him with an opportunity to stay in the Premier League.

As Standard Sport reported, all options are on the table for Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta, and if the Frenchman was to leave, Palace would potentially be left looking for cover for Jorgen Strand Larsen.

#1828. Ghana vs Somalia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 10 Nov 2026 20:14, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 20:24

Ghana will be desperate to breathe life into their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they play host to Somalia at the Essipong Sports Stadium in the first of their Group C double-header on Thursday.

Having lost their first two matches, both nations are left with little room for mistakes and know Thursday’s result could prove decisive in shaping up their qualifying ambitions, and this makes for an exciting contest in Sekondi-Takoradi.

Two games into the race for a spot in the 2027 AFCON, Ghana find themselves amongst nine sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, with the federation parting ways with Portuguese coach Carlos Queiroz and opting for a change in ideas in the dugout.

Coming off the back of a round-of-32 defeat against Colombia in the World Cup back in June, the Black Stars kicked off their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-0 loss against Ivory Coast on September 24, with Malick Yalcouye and Franck Kessie netting on either side of half-time to hand the Elephants all three points.

Playing in front of the home supporters five days later, Ghana failed to make home advantage count in matchday two, when they fell to a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Gambia after squandering a two-goal lead at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Ernest Nuamah and Felix Afena-Gyan hit the target to put Ghana in the driver’s seat, but strikes from Muhammed Badamosi, Omar Colley, and a second-half brace from Konyaspor striker Ebrima Colley turned the game on its head for Gambia.

The four-time African champions have now gone eight straight games without a win in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, a run which saw them miss out on the 2025 AFCON, failing to feature in the continental showpiece for the first time since 2004.

Now tasked with restoring confidence and flipping the script, interim coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren faces a must-win assignment on Thursday as Ghana seek to avoid missing back-to-back AFCON tournaments for the first time since their three successive absences in 1986, 1988 and 1990.

Like the home side, Somalia journey to the Essipong Sports Stadium with the same urgent need for a result if they are to turn their fortunes around and secure a first-ever qualification for the Africa Cup of Nations.

Having edged out Eswatini and Mauritius in the preliminary phase, the Ocean Stars fell to a 2-1 loss against Gambia in the Group C opener on September 25, with Ebrima Colley and Muhammed Badamosi netting on either side of Bilal Njie’s 72nd-minute equaliser to hand the hosts all three points at the Independence Stadium.

While there were positives to take from the defeat against Gambia, Somalia were left spitting feathers four days later, when they fell to a 2-0 defeat against Ivory Coast through strikes from Yann Gboho and Bazoumana Toure in the final six minutes at the Stade Felix Houphouet-Boigny.

Yusuf Ali’s men demonstrated their ability to rise to the occasion against quality opposition last time out when they pushed Ivory Coast to the limit, and they will have reason to believe they can upset the odds against a Ghana side currently far from convincing.

Ghana Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Somalia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Newly-appointed Ghana boss Bjorkegren has called up 26 players to the squad for October’s double-header with Somalia, including the Premier League trio of Abdul Fatawu Issahaku, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ibrahim Osman.

Having missed the first two qualifying matches through a groin problem, Jordan Ayew has been recalled to the squad, and the nation’s captain will hope his leadership and wealth of experience can count for something.

The Black Stars will also be lifted by the return of Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus, who is set to make his first international appearance of the year after missing the World Cup through an injury.

Manchester City forward Antoine Semenyo misses out through a knee injury, while 31-year-old defender Jan Gyamerah, who made his debut against Mexico on May 26, is also ruled out through a muscle problem.

Before their late collapse, Somalia held their own against a superior and more experienced Ivory Coast side last time out, and we expect Ali to name a similar XI on Thursday, with Mohamed Mohamed, Abel Gigli, Ali Omar and Faisal Othman shielding 20-year-old Ibrahim Ahmed Hussein between the sticks.

With eight goal involvements in his last nine matches for club and country, KFUM Oslo striker Nije is currently in fine form, and the 28-year-old striker should lead the Ocean Stars attack once again, while Mohamed Omar, Abdi Sharif and Mukhtar Suleiman should team up in midfield.

Ati-Zigi; Seidu, Adjetey, Salisu, Mensah; Partey, Yirenkyi; Kudus, Abdul Fatawu, Ayew; Thomas-Asante

Hussein; Mohamed, Gigli, A. Omar, Osman; M. Omar, Sharif, Suleiman; Addo, Njie, Hassan

Despite the quality in their rank, Ghana have failed an impression in the AFCON qualifiers so far, but victory on Thursday could provide the spark needed to turn their Group C campaign around.

Although Somalia have shown glimpses of their potential in their opening two matches, the difference in individual quality could prove a decisive factor here, with Ghana tipped to come away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

#1827. Bellingham grateful for Beckham, Wright support

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jude Bellingham has opened up on the constant support he has received from fellow England icons David Beckham and Ian Wright.

Since his breakthrough into the Three Lions' setup, Bellingham has transformed into one of England's key players.

He scored seven goals at the 2026 World Cup as Thomas Tuchel's side finished third, the most ever by an England player at a single edition of the tournament.

Bellingham has scored 14 goals in 60 caps, though the 23-year-old has at times come in for criticism from the media, while he also butted heads with Tuchel last season.

There were suggestions in the build-up to the World Cup that Bellingham's place in the lineup should be at risk, though he silenced his doubters with some talismanic performances, including scoring twice in a memorable win over Mexico at the Estadio Azteca.

And Bellingham is grateful for the support of Wright and former England captain Beckham.

"I feel mature in a football context because I've played nearly 400 games, but in a life context I don't feel that mature now, to be honest," Bellingham told British Vogue.

"Sometimes it's not the message, but it's the messenger that makes it more valuable. You've got someone on your side who knows what the score is."

Building the intensity https://t.co/VRAcurccH4

Wright has publicly defended Bellingham, and the Real Madrid star said: "I always get really nervous when he messages me.

"I always think, 'What have they said about me now?' I always see him at the England games and will give him a hug or blow him a kiss."

Bellingham's younger brother, Jobe, has been named in the England squad for the upcoming Nations League clashes with Croatia and Spain.

Should Jobe feature while his elder sibling is on the pitch, they will become the first pair of brothers to feature for England together since 2007 (Gary and Phil Neville).

They will become the 22nd brothers to play for England overall.

Croatia are England's opponents at Wembley on Thursday, with Harry Kane set to win his record-breaking 126th cap for the Three Lions, who then visit Spain on Sunday.

#1826. The first players Mauricio Pochettino could sign as Manchester United manager

Mauricio Pochettino looks set to become the next Manchester United manager, with Michael Carrick finally set to be given the chop at Old Trafford.

But Pochettino will run into an immediate problem: the squad is not capable of playing his high-pressing brand of football.

The answer? The transfer market. Pochettino will likely require a complete overhaul, starting in the January window. Man Utd have attempted to refresh different areas of the squad over the last two summers, spending hundreds of millions on the attack in 2025 before replacing the midfield during the summer just gone.

The defence is crying out for investment, quite literally in the case of Lisando Martinez, who attacked Man Utd’s hierarchy over a failure to recruit properly during the summer.

Man Utd require new full-backs, frequently playing right-backs on the left and then requiring a centre-half to fill in on the right.

So who could, and should, Pochettino turn to in January?

Swashbuckling Antonee Robinson has become a trusted lieutenant for Pochettino in the US national team. The Fulham left-back is in his prime at 29, and would bring proven Premier League quality and knowledge of Pochettino’s approach.

Another American could help Pochettino improve Manchester United’s defence. Alex Freeman was handed an international debut by the Argentine in 2025, and has already racked up 26 caps. The defender has also been tracked by the Red Devils previously.

His displays for the USMNT and in the MLS for Orlando City led Freeman to join La Liga outfit Villarreal in January, helping El Submarino Amarillo qualify for the Champions League.

Under Inigo Perez - who, like Pochettino, is a disciple of Marcelo Bielsa - Freeman has proven he can play high-intensity football in a host of positions. A natural right-back, Freeman has played as both a full-back and wing-back on either flank, the wide center-back in a three-man defence, and has even been deployed further up the pitch as a winger.

Lewis Hall was a target for Man Utd during the last summer window, only for the Newcastle left-back to end any possible move by signing a new contract on Tyneside.

Ratcliffe and INEOS should be ashamed at how they are running Man Utd

Kane, Palmer and Paz: Pochettino's dream Man Utd XI revealed

'Chosen one' or 'cooked'? Man Utd fans split on Pochettino move

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

However, with Newcastle also struggling this term, Man Utd could try to tempt the 22-year-old to Old Trafford. Hall’s age is a better fit for the profile of player Man Utd are trying to build their squad around.

One defensive recruit the club have had their eyes on for a while is Jarrad Branthwaite. The Everton centre-back first popped up on the Red Devils’ radar in 2024, with the Toffees rejecting two bids for the England international.

Man Utd have been credited with renewing their interest in the 24-year-old, who has shaken off injury concerns to become a reliable member of David Moyes’ Everton squad.

Nico Paz pulled the strings as Como shocked Man Utd 4-1 in the Champions League last month, and the former Real Madrid youngster is beginning to attract attention from the biggest clubs in Europe.

Paz has reportedly been identified as the successor for Bruno Fernandes, with both playing their best football in a free role as an attacking midfielder.

Man Utd fans will be pleased to hear that Paz’s attacking output is similar to Fernandes, but with an increased defensive actions - ranking in the 34th percentile for attacking midfielders across Europe’s top five leagues this season. For comparison, Fernandes is only in the 17th percentile.

Real Madrid hold a buyback clause, which could cause a potential stumbling block for any move.

Despite investing in their strikeforce two summers ago, Man Utd have resorted to playing wingers and midfielders up top. Marquee striker signing Benjamin Sesko has endured an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford, while Joshua Zirkzee almost left at the end of the last transfer window.

Pochettino will require a reliable back-up to Sesko, either to change games or simply keep Slovenian on his toes. Man Utd will hope not to spend too much on a player of such profile, but two USMNT players could fit the bill.

As the striker will lead the press for Pochettino, the former Tottenham boss will require a keen runner with the ability to score goals. Ricardo Pepi is a strong candidate: extremely fast and hard-working, the 23-year-old has grabbed 49 goals in 113 appearances for PSV, including six goals in the Champions League.

Bringing Pepi to Manchester shouldn’t break the bank, nor would signing Folarin Balogun. Monaco hoped to shift the American on during the last transfer window due to financial constraints, which means a cut-price deal could be arranged in January.

#1825. Arsenal given Ezri Konsa injury update after defender skips England training

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Thomas Tuchel has confirmed that Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence will both miss England’s Nations League clash at home to Croatia through injury.

Konsa has been managing his fitness after taking a hit to his knee during Arsenal’s 2-1 win away to Slavia Prague.

The 29-year-old three days later played the full 90 minutes as Arsenal narrowly beat Hull, but has been following an individual training programme since linking up with England.

Konsa was absent as the Three Lions trained at Tottenham’s training ground on Wednesday afternoon, along with Spence, who has struggled for fitness since leaving Spurs for Inter Milan over the summer.

Asked about the pair, Tuchel confirmed he did not want to risk further injury by playing either of them against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

“It’s my understanding at the moment that they will be both available but we will not take the risk. For tomorrow, both out for tomorrow,” Tuchel said in his pre-match press conference.

“You saw it, they were not in training. They follow their own programme, and the understanding and the hope and the belief, I would say, is that they’re both in individual training on Friday, team training on Saturday and match ready on Sunday.”

England are looking to top their Nations League group, starting with the visit of Croatia. They then take on World Champions Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid this weekend.

Tuchel’s side enjoyed a successful international break in September, winning three of their four games, including a 7-0 demolition of Croatia in Rijeka.

#1824. Non-league footballer in stable condition after collapsing in warm-up and being rushed to hospital, leading to match being abandoned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:35 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:08 EST, 7 November 2026

Truro City's match against Folkestone Invicta was abandoned due to a medical emergency on Saturday after a footballer collapsed during the warm-up.

Yassine En-Neyah, 26, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing while preparing with his team-mates on the pitch. It was later confirmed he was in a stable condition.

The former Nottingham Forest academy youngster had been named among the substitutes to face Folkestone in the National League South game in Kent.

A club statement on Saturday read: 'Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.

'Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.'

The club added a welcome on Saturday night, saying: 'He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation.

Truro City's clash with Folkestone Invicta has been abandoned due to a medical emergency

Yassine En-Neyah - pictured before the game - was named on the bench to face Folkestone

Club Statement:Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed. Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.We will… pic.twitter.com/IyiF2VIFMz

'The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

'Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.'

Truro City's players had earlier gathered around the rear of the ambulance where En-Neyah was being treated to shield him from view.

The Moroccan-born former Republic of Ireland youth international began his career at Nottingham Forest, making his professional debut in January 2020 as a substitute during an FA Cup third-round clash against Chelsea.

After being released by Forest in 2021, the winger has played for multiple non-league sides including Shelbourne, Waterford and Maldon & Tipree.

Having briefly represented Truro in 2023, En-Neyah returned to the Tinners for a second spell in 2024, where he has remained since.

When he signed his new Truro contract last season, En-Neyah admitted he didn't think twice about the decision to stay.

'Truro's been my home for the last couple of seasons and it was a very easy decision,' he told BBC Radio Cornwall.

'I feel home so I just want to continue working hard and help the club achieve greater things.

'It wasn't a case of having to think about it, it was just a matter of getting it done and continuing to work hard and do well for the club and for myself.'

#1822. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta quoted '£67m' for Bundesliga winger Gunners could have signed for £50m in summer

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 20:41

RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa will cost Arsenal in the region of £67m if they are to sign him in the January transfer window, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners have entered the international break as the Premier League leaders, with their 1-0 win against Hull City on Saturday increasing their lead to five points.

Despite his team's position, Mikel Arteta may hold some concerns about his side's attack given they have scored just 15 goals in 10 games.

Arsenal have been linked with a number of wingers in recent months, including Leipzig forward Nusa, who was reportedly a target in the summer.

The Evening Standard claim that the Gunners' decision to not sign Nusa for £50m means they will have to pay at least £67m in January for his signature.

Nusa is enjoying his best ever season for Leipzig, with the left-winger having scored six goals and provided eight assists in all competitions.

The forward only managed to score five goals and provide four assists in 2025-26, while he netted five goals and provided six assists in 2024-25.

Nusa is 21 and has room for improvement, but his pace, finishing and dribbling qualities could make him a valuable asset for Arteta in the years to come.

The good news for Arsenal is that Leipzig have a history of sanctioning deals at the right price, though it remains to be seen if they would be willing to accept a lower fee in the winter considering they are competing for Champions League football.

The Gunners have long been criticised for their style of play, though Arteta proved last season that his side are capable of winning silverware despite their dull approach.

However, the club are only on track to score 57 goals in the league this season, and they would become the lowest-scoring title winners in the history of the Premier League if they finished first.

Arteta's side should still be seen as favourites for the title, but the signing of someone like Nusa in January would help push them over the line.

#1821. Why Manchester United face a race against time to confirm Mauricio Pochettino appointment

Manchester United could be in a race against time to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager.

Carrick sack news LIVE: Man Utd latest as Pochettino accepts job offer

The first players Pochettino could sign as Man Utd manager

Ratcliffe and INEOS should be ashamed at how they are running Man Utd

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

It has been widely reported that the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss is in line to become the next head coach at Old Trafford, with talks under way and personal terms close to being finalised.

Pochettino would replace Michael Carrick, who remains in post but is expected to be sacked following a meeting of the United hierarchy that is due to take place in Monaco on Wednesday.

It is understood that a final decision to dismiss Carrick has yet to be taken, but that CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are likely to recommend to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that a change is made in an attempt to halt United’s alarming run of form that has seen them win just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches and sit in the relegation zone heading into the November international break.

Pochettino has emerged as United’s No1 option to succeed Carrick, with the club understood to be willing to pay the $10million (£7.5m) release clause in his contract with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), which was only extended until 2030 after this summer’s World Cup on home soil.

The Argentine has spoken to United on multiple occasions in the past and is known to be keen on the job, moving clear of the likes of Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte in the race.

However, United will likely have to move quickly to get the agreement finalised, with the USA having an important two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie coming up.

They initially take on Haiti in Miami on Saturday, before playing the second fixture in Cincinnati next Wednesday. The USMNT close 2026 with a friendly against Jamaica in Fort Lauderdale on December 13.

The first leg against Haiti has been relocated from Kingston in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”, with Haiti having been unable to stage home matches in their own country since 2021.

Pochettino has been in charge of the USMNT since succeeding Gregg Berhalter in the aftermath of the 2024 Copa America tournament, finishing as a runner-up in last year’s Gold Cup and also leading the team to the last 16 of a World Cup co-hosted by the United States earlier this year.

The USMNT, United and Pochettino will surely all look to have the situation resolved before those games against Haiti, with struggling United returning from the international break with a huge game away against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

Pochettino is due to address reporters on Friday ahead of the first leg against Haiti in a pre-match press conference, though the USA have cancelled media access scheduled for Wednesday in observance of Veterans Day.

#1819. Cucurella defends Vinicius Jr over Diomande comparison as Real Madrid pause eight-game winning run

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 20:52

Marc Cucurella has defended Vinicius Junior amid the Brazilian’s difficult start to the season, insisting that team-mate Yan Diomande does not help him more defensively than the Real Madrid forward does. Real Madrid have paused an eight-game winning run for the international break, during the best spell under boss Jose Mourinho, and are hoping Vinicius rediscovers his form with Brazil under Carlo Ancelotti. Cucurella shares that wish.

Speaking on the Cope radio programme El Partidazo, the Spanish left-back was asked about the poor start to the season of Vinicius, who has just one goal and three assists in 12 matches. The decline in his form, together with a suspension that kept him out of the last four La Liga games, has led to the meteoric rise of Diomande, who has made a difference on the left side.

Beyond four goals and four assists in 16 matches, the Ivory Coast forward has been praised for his tactical commitment, helping Cucurella with defensive recovery. But the Real Madrid number 17 rejects the idea that Diomande helps him more with marking than the Brazilian does.

‘I do not think he helps me more, I think he is more visible,’ Cucurella said. ‘Diomande runs back and is everywhere. Vinicius goes back three times and then, the fourth time he does not run, the ball is played in. If Vini scored three goals per game, nobody would say anything to him.’

Days after his signing from Chelsea was announced in late June, the defender told Radio Marca that he ‘did not mind’ if Vinicius ‘does not track back or help in defence’, because he wanted the number seven energised to have an impact in the final third with goals. Cucurella also told Vinicius that he would do all the ‘dirty work’ for him.

Despite that consent, the forward has helped with the compactness without the ball, following the Portuguese boss’s guidance. The main problem is that, in possession, the 26-year-old has not shown the same efficiency as in recent years in dribbles in one-on-one situations and in decision-making.

Like other figures at Real Madrid, the Spaniard came out in defence of Vinicius, considering a dip in form natural after consecutive seasons among the best players in the world. The left-back also insisted that Vinicius has been working behind the scenes to react and regain his prominence, which he considers fundamental to Mourinho’s success in 2026-27.

‘Vinicius is a player who has been performing at a spectacular level for five years, so it is understandable that he is going through a difficult phase now,’ Cucurella continued. ‘I see that he is motivated and works hard in training, and that is what matters.’

‘The most important thing for us is that he returns to his best level, because if he is at his peak, we have a great team,’ he concluded.

#1818. England confirm how Harry Kane's record-breaking appearance will be celebrated

The Football Association have confirmed how they will mark Harry Kane breaking the all-time England appearance record on Thursday.

Kane is set to start against Croatia in the Nations League and, in doing so, will make his 126th appearance and overtake Peter Shilton to become the most-capped men’s player in the history of the national team.

The England captain is to receive a special commemoration before the game, with Shilton to be involved, and the player will also present his Ballon d’Or trophy, won late last month in London.

Kane is already the nation’s all-time top scorer. He has scored 91 goals for England. The record was previously held by Wayne Rooney, who scored 53 goals for the Three Lions.

An FA statement on Wednesday afternoon read: “Harry Kane is set to be recognised as England men’s record appearance maker at Wembley Stadium on Thursday.

“The Three Lions captain is expected to play in the UEFA Nations League tie against Croatia which will take him to 126 appearances for his nation.

“A special pre-match presentation is planned to honour the historic milestone with current joint-record holder Peter Shilton to lead that activity.”

The statement continued: “Shilton has held the record since 1989 and finished his 20-year England career with 125 caps. The legendary goalkeeper is in line to formally mark Kane becoming the first Three Lions men’s player to reach 126 caps.

“Kane’s achievement in being crowned the world’s best player by winning the prestigious Ballon d’Or will also acknowledged on the night.”

#1817. Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 14:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:21 EST, 7 November 2026

This run will not be about the verdicts. This cannot be about the verdicts. Footballers do not care about these things, the stuff out of their control. Besides, all of them are earning cut-price transfers elsewhere were Manchester City to suffer relegation anyway. And cut-price fees mean bulkier salaries.

So to them the current climate, the circumstances around City – their recent history and their immediate future – does not overly matter. Sure, there might be the odd one who is slightly more philosophical and inquisitive about appeals and appendices but the majority won't be giving it much or any thought.

City insist on their innocence publicly and privately; until that changes, their players and Enzo Maresca carry on regardless. There were the usual jeers here, there were ditties about cheating, but that surely cannot affect them.

Instead, the performances over the past few weeks, this a third consecutive Premier League defeat and now sinking six points adrift of Arsenal, cannot be excused by the findings of an independent commission. The problems are football problems.

This is a squad who appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game. Namely how to build from the back – and that is prompting individual mistakes. It happened against Ipswich Town and at Aston Villa. On the river Trent, it was no different.

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story.

Man City are a squad who now appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story

Three defeats in a row have seen Enzo Maresca's side slip six points behind leaders Arsenal

Too many errors. Too much arm waving. Too much feeling sorry for themselves when decisions go elsewhere. Oliver Glasner is not stupid, he will have seen examples of this play out in parts of City's victories as well as reverses.

As Liam Delap raced into the corner to celebrate his second with 17 minutes left – a huge day in his career against the club which moulded him – Glasner was dashing down the touchline with unbridled joy.

Nottingham Forest (5-2-2-1): Sels 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 65, 6), Cunha 8, Milenkovic 8, Murillo 7, Williams 8; Yates 8 (Sangare 79), Schlager 8; McAtee 7 (Ndoye 65, 6), Gibbs-White 7; Delap 9 (Jesus 87)

Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Nunes 46, 7), Gvardiol 4 (O'Reilly 46, 6); Anderson 5; Ndiaye 6, Cherki 6, Fernandez 4 (Foden 78), Doku 6; Haaland 5

Forest displays have deserved more than their points total so far and this was vindication for their fifth manager in 14 months, who suggested he fancied sampling Nottingham’s nightlife afterwards. Delap was exceptional, some personal redemption after criticism.

The way in which Glasner nudged James McAtee further forward, stationed higher from the off in order to pressurise the visitors, spoke to an idea that City arrived here ready to be ruffled and have been wearing a look of fragility.

By the time this was eight minutes shy of half time and McAtee was nicking possession from Elliot Anderson, drawing a foul that sparked another onslaught on Gianluigi Donnarumma's box, Forest were already two clear – and had been for some time. Phil Foden warmed up on the touchline, laughing and hugging with Callum Hudson-Odoi.

Forest preyed on City insecurities. A midfield structure that is simply not working at the moment, easily railroaded. A defence allergic to the basics and an epidemic of individual mistakes – either as a result of nervousness or blase attitude on the ball.

Straight to the mistakes. A real collection, these: the first in the fifth minute and the others 13 minutes afterwards. Jair Cunha wheeled away after picking Josko Gvardiol's pocket, meandering forward into the box and side-footing into the far corner largely unchallenged. Gvardiol seemed to have the air of a man who felt invincible when gathering possession before being eased off it.

Later, as Delap thundered forward 45 yards unchecked to hammer past Donnarumma, you wondered about the communication between these City players. Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye left things to each other near halfway, Xaver Schlager gave his thanks – finding Delap – and the City academy graduate bulldozed clear. Marc Guehi waved him through, Ruben Dias dithered and Maresca bowed his head.

Liam Delap was exceptional for Nottingham Forest, some personal redemption after criticism

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes. Dias looked aghast at Guehi, who was then hooked at the break alongside Gvardiol. Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both stood in the centre circle, hands on hips.

It later emerged via replays that Anderson had been arguing with Abdukodir Khusanov in the build-up to Forest's opener as well, proof that City were nowhere near close to producing what was expected when on the ball in their own half.

Glasner had the weapons at his disposal to make this work but even the Austrian must have been surprised at the way in which they tickled City's soft underbelly. They had not scored at the City Ground all season. All change when owner Evangelos Marinakis made his first trip to see a game since Glasner's appointment, which felt particularly handy, with Yates having delivered a spinetingling dressing room speech pre-match.

Anger permeated the eyes of some City players as the whistle went. Cherki stormed down the tunnel, animatedly discussing how to play through Forest with Fernandez when they re-emerged.

Their lifeline came after 52 minutes, a Ryan Yates deflection from Jeremy Doku's cross sitting up for Cherki to hammer home a half-volley off the bar. Doku soon almost squeezed another effort past Matz Sels and the mood shifted, City briefly creeping menacingly like the monsters they are portrayed as.

Maresca had introduced Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, with both affecting the upturn. An admission of selection errors, perhaps, although O'Reilly is managing an ongoing back issue and is set for therapy on it over the international break.

City will need some of that as a collective. Delap won the ball inside his own third, gliding past Anderson, and Forest's explosive counter ended with Delap spearing a shot in off the post after Morgan Gibbs-White carried possession unopposed for 60 yards. Delirium, Glasner darting to the corner flag.

The quirk of this is that City's failings mean Manchester United drop into the bottom three.

Maresca criticised Manchester City’s lack of fight but insisted that City created enough chances to leave with something despite admitting his players were physically second best.

‘In the first half we were not good enough - we didn't match the intensity that these kind of games require,’ Maresca said.

‘If you are not able to win the second balls then you struggle. You have to match the desire to win second balls and duels, otherwise it is not good. When you lost balls the way we did and cannot recover immediately, it’s a matter of winning duels.’

Maresca has a two-week international break to rake over the issues affecting his side and believes time away could do the squad good.

The Italian added: ‘When you lose a game you always want to go again immediately to try to win games but I think that this international break, the last one until March, is also good for the players.

‘We didn't match the intensity. We need to understand the reason why and try to avoid the next games. There is no panic. We need to understand but no panic.’

Maresca revealed that defenders Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol asked to come off at half time with injuries, while Forest out-ran his team by 6km on the night.

‘If you want to win against City, you need to do this,’ Oliver Glasner said after recording his first home win. ‘Credit to Liam, these strikes are something you have or you don't have.

‘It can be a turning point but we have to prove it. The way we performed today should give us confidence.’

City winger Jeremy Doku could not explain why they could not deal with Forest before half time.

‘We are used to playing every two days - that's not a reason,’ Doku said. ‘If you ask me for the reason for our first half I don't know.

‘We reacted too late. We need to be fresh minds, start again and analyse what we can do better and move forward. The international break comes at the right moment for us to analyse and come back refreshed.’

#1816. USA confirm cancellation as 'Mauricio Pochettino agrees to become Manchester United manager'

The United States have cancelled their media access day, amid reports of a verbal agreement between head coach Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United.

It has been widely reported that framework is in place for United to appoint Pochettino should current head coach Michael Carrick, as expected, be relieved of his duties, with the club sitting in the Premier League relegation zone on the back of their worst start to a season since 1986.

Pochettino is understood to be interested in the Old Trafford post, and according to The Athletic, his representatives spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with the club, with no major obstacles expected and a final agreement expected.

However, the possibility of the USMNT squad being asked to comment on the news of Argentine’s potential exit has been removed as US Soccer confirmed the planned media access with players scheduled for Wednesday had been cancelled in observance of Veterans Day.

With that said, Pochettino is due to address reporters on Friday in a pre-match press conference to preview USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie first leg against Haiti.

According to reports, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s USMT contract worth $10million (£7.44m) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

The 54-year-old has not managed in the Premier League since a short spell with Chelsea during the 2023-24 season, though has previously teased a return to England.

“I miss the football scene in England. I love the country, its culture, the football culture,” he said in an interview with L’Equipe.

“For anyone with a competitive spirit who wants to measure themselves against others and test their limits, it's the ideal place. Here, you have to give your best constantly.”

If Pochettino is appointed by United within the next few days, his first game in charge will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

#1814. Barcelona Women vs Arsenal Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 21:06, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:27

Arsenal Women will travel to Camp Nou for Thursday's highly anticipated meeting with reigning European Champions Barcelona Women.

The Gunners are sitting in fifth spot in the Women's Champions League league phase, while the Catalan giants are flying high at the top of the standings with a perfect record.

Barcelona have made the perfect start to their bid to win a fifth UWCL title, having won their opening three league phase games by a combined 19-2 scoreline.

After comfortably dispatching Paris FC and Roma, Barcelona made light work of their clash against Koge on matchday three, with Claudia Pina netting a brace in an emphatic 8-0 victory in Denmark.

Barcelona returned to Liga F action with a 4-0 success against fellow Catalan side Badalona, before they eased to a 5-1 victory in Sunday's meeting with Madrid CFF, moving them four points clear of second-placed Real Madrid at the top of the standings.

Those two league wins have helped Barcelona build a four-game winning run since suffering a surprise 2-1 away loss against Real Sociedad on October 18.

While they experienced a blip on their travels, Barcelona have won all six of their competitive home games this season, scoring at least five goals in five of those victories.

The Blaugrana have also won 33 of their 35 UWCL home games (D1, L1), including each of their last 11 European home assignments since losing 1-0 to Chelsea in the first leg of their semi-final tie in April 2024.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have struggled for consistency in domestic action this season, with Renee Slegers's side sitting in sixth spot and six points adrift of the top three after recording three wins, four draws and two defeats in nine Women's Super League games.

Having taken seven points from their three European games, the Gunners are at least in a better position in the Women's Champions League, even if their first two performances were far from convincing.

Arsenal required a 93rd-minute penalty to see off Koge on matchday one, before they spurned a goal lead in a frustrating 2-2 draw against Paris FC in the French capital.

The Gunners at least made light work of their home game against Benfica, which saw Alessia Russo net a hat-trick in a commanding 3-0 victory at Meadow Park to become the leading English scorer in UWCL history with 23 goals.

Russo went on to score in a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa before registering a brace in Sunday's 2-1 away win over Liverpool, meaning she has now scored nine goals in Arsenal's last seven competitive matches.

The in-form forward will be hoping to continue her impressive form in Thursday's fixture, as Arsenal look for a repeat of the memorable 1-0 victory they recorded in their most recent meeting with Barcelona in the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon.

Arsenal Women Women's Champions League form:

Barcelona boss Pere Romeu remains without the services of Laia Aleixandri, Kika Nazareth and Vicky Lopez due to injury.

Kerolin has also been added to the injury list, having been ruled out for around four weeks with a calf problem.

Renee van Asten, Patri Guijarro and Aitana Bonmati could all come into the side after dropping down to the bench for the win over Madrid CFF.

As for the visitors, they are expected to be without Mariona Caldentey, Selina Cerci, Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang, while there are doubts surrounding the availability of Stina Blackstenius and Chloe Kelly.

Defender Taylor Hinds is also an injury concern after being withdrawn in the closing stages of the win over Liverpool.

Former Barcelona full-back Ona Batlle is expected to return to the squad after sitting out Sunday’s game with a knock.

While Arsenal are yet to lose in Europe this season, there is no tougher European fixture than facing Barcelona at the Camp Nou, and considering the home side's impressive home record, we think the reigning UWCL champions will pick up a comfortable victory.

#1813. Harry Kane sends Manchester United message over Mauricio Pochettino move

Harry Kane has paid tribute to former manager Mauricio Pochettino as the Ballon d’Or winner prepares to break England’s all-time men’s appearance record.

Kane is set to surpass Peter Shilton as England’s all-time appearance-maker in senior men’s football on Thursday night when he features against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley.

The Bayern Munich striker, recently crowned the best player in the world and closing in on 100 goals for the Three Lions, will earn his 126th cap, and a special pre-match presentation is planned to honour the historic milestone.

Kane has come a long way since his breakthrough campaign at Tottenham during the 2014/15 season, when he notched 21 Premier League goals, as Pochettino’s young team narrowly missed out on Champions League qualification.

Following a six-game goalless run at the start of the next campaign, Kane was famously dubbed as a one-season wonder, but he credits Pochettino’s guidance with helping him defy his critics to push on and become Spurs’ and England’s all-time record goalscorer.

“Yeah, me and Mauricio obviously have a fantastic relationship. I think, again, I mentioned him as one of the coaches that had a big impact on my career and definitely my development,” Kane said.

“At that stage of my career, I needed his guidance and the way he pushed me, not just on the pitch but off the pitch as well, was really, really helpful.”

Pochettino is currently in charge of the USA men’s national team, but Standard Sport understands that Manchester United have checked on his availability as they potentially look for a successor to Michael Carrick.

Carrick is under fire and at serious risk of losing his job with United currently in the Premier League relegation zone, and they have long held an interest in Pochettino.

“He’s managed the biggest clubs in the world. So yeah, from my point of view, I can’t speak highly enough of him,” Kane continued.

“So yeah, we’ll have to wait and see what happens. But I know he’s a great guy, but also a fantastic manager.”

#1812. Germany hoping to tee up Berlin final versus Netherlands, says Treu

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Germany's motivation for beating Serbia on Friday is to set up a do-or-die clash with the Netherlands in Berlin next week, right-back Philipp Treu has declared.

Jurgen Klopp's first international break in charge of his country was a mixed one, as Germany conceded a late equaliser against the Netherlands, then lost 1-0 at home to Greece.

A 2-0 victory over Serbia got them back on track somewhat in Nations League Group A2, but after a goalless draw in the reverse fixture against Greece, their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals are in the balance.

With five points on the board, Germany are three adrift of both Greece and the Oranje, ahead of their visit to Belgrade on matchday five.

A defeat in Serbia could eliminate Germany with a game to spare, and even with a win, they would need a positive result against the Netherlands – at the Olympiastadion on Monday – to reach the last eight.

But for Treu and the rest of Klopp's squad, it is just about taking things one match at a time.

"We have an open group ahead of us," he told reporters. "We're going into the Serbia game with the will to win and work towards a final in Berlin. That's the focus for now.

"We also know that it won't be an easy game in Serbia, but we want to come out with a positive result."

Treu was one of several uncapped players to be called up by Klopp during the last international break and went on to make his first three Germany appearances during that period.

A post shared by German Football (@germanfootball_dfb)

The 25-year-old has enjoyed a strong start to the campaign, with Freiburg sitting third in the Bundesliga despite selling star midfielder Johan Manzambi to Aston Villa off the back of their Europa League final appearance last season.

Treu ranks second, among players to have made more than five Bundesliga appearances in 2026-27, for ground duel success rate (77.8%, 28/36), behind Werder Bremen's Amos Pieper (78.1%, 25/32).

And now, he is aiming to gatecrash Klopp's starting line-up, though he acknowledges there is fierce competition for places in every position.

"It's an incredible honour to be here at all," he added. "What did me a lot of good at the beginning was that I already knew a lot of players; like Nico Schlotterbeck, for example, who gave me a great welcome.

"The experienced players, in particular, have tried to talk to the newcomers.

"I just try to give everything in training. The competition is so tough here. We face up to it, and we will benefit from the fact that we push each other.

"I believe that the wingers have a lot of freedom here. As a full-back, it is particularly important to give the wingers support, with an overlapping run or by leaving the middle free so that the wingers can move inside.

"Defensively, too, it is always about the cooperation between the two players."

#1811. Chelsea get major new Josh Acheampong injury update as statement issued

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have been given a further hint at the possible severity of Josh Acheampong’s injury.

Acheampong missed Sunday’s 1-0 defeat at Sunderland in the Premier League, where Enzo Le Fee’s penalty was enough to move the Black Cats off the foot of the table.

And now he has withdrawn from the England Under-21s squad and returned to Chelsea, meaning he will play no part in England U21s' upcoming fixtures against Portugal and France in the coming week.

A statement reads: “Josh Acheampong and James Beadle have withdrawn from the England men's under-21 squad ahead of their upcoming fixtures against Portugal and France.

“Lee Carsley's side are scheduled to face both nations at Ashton Gate in Bristol during the November international window.

“Acheampong has withdrawn from the squad having been absent for Chelsea’s trip to Sunderland whilst Beadle was substituted during half time of Birmingham City's victory over Lincoln City and subsequently missed Blues’ next two fixtures.

“Both players are now unavailable for the Young Lions' double-header.”

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso was asked ahead of the Sunderland game why Acheampong was absent from the matchday squad.

He replied: “He is recovering from a minor thing. He missed the fitness to be ready for today but we are expecting that he will be back after the international break. It’s a pity because he was in a good moment.

“There are situations. Yesterday Josh felt something and he was not fit to play. So we are shorter in options and we need to go through this time.

“Even when we win, or when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting to have them back because they are important.

“Now we need to use the time to recover them, but with the players we have, we have to get ready for the next one.”

#1810. Ivory Coast vs Gambia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 10 Nov 2026 21:27, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 21:28

Ivory Coast and The Gambia will be looking to maintain their perfect starts to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they meet at Stade de la Paix in Bouake on Thursday evening.

Both teams have collected six points from their opening two Group C matches, and Thursday's encounter represents the first of two meetings between the sides in five days, with the return fixture scheduled to take place in The Gambia on November 17.

Ivory Coast have made an encouraging start under returning head coach Herve Renard, who began his second spell in charge with two wins from two competitive matches before suffering a friendly defeat to Cameroon.

His return opened with a 2-0 victory over Ghana, with Malick Yalcouye opening the scoring before Franck Kessie converted a second-half penalty, and the Elephants followed that result with another 2-0 win against Somalia, as Bazoumana Toure and Yann Gboho found the net.

The Elephants are yet to concede in the qualifying campaign and will be hoping to maintain that defensive record against The Gambia on Thursday, having won their last four meetings with the Scorpions while scoring nine goals and conceding none.

Ivory Coast also boast an impressive home record in this fixture, having won all three previous meetings on their own soil, scoring eight goals without conceding.

While the Elephants have been particularly solid defensively at the start of this campaign, The Gambia's attacking firepower has been central to their own impressive opening, with the Scorpions scoring six goals across their first two qualifiers.

They began with a 2-1 victory over Somalia before producing an impressive comeback to beat Ghana 4-2 away from home, with Ebrima Colley scoring three goals across the two matches, including a brace against the Black Stars.

The West African side will be looking to make it three consecutive victories, a feat they have not achieved in the last five years, with that run predating Johnny McKinstry's appointment as head coach in June 2024.

However, one concern for the visitors will be their lack of defensive solidity, having failed to keep a clean sheet in their last five matches, although they have managed to score 10 goals during that period.

Ivory Coast Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Gambia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Amad Diallo has returned to the Ivory Coast squad after overcoming an injury concern, providing Renard with another attacking option for the double-header.

However, the Elephants will be without Odilon Kossounou and Guela Doue, who are both sidelined through injury, while Wilfried Singo, Simon Adingra, Evann Guessand and Sebastien Haller have not been included in the squad.

The Gambia have been boosted by the returns of Musa Barrow and Yankuba Minteh, who have both recovered from the injuries that kept them out of the September qualifiers.

Alieu Fadera and Adama Sidibeh are unavailable through injury, while James Gomez has not been included in the final squad.

Jesper Ceesay and Suleiman Camara have also withdrawn because of injuries, with Saidou Khan and Salieu Drammeh called up as their replacements.

The Gambia's attacking form makes it difficult to envisage another straightforward clean sheet for Ivory Coast, but the hosts have shown greater defensive control and possess enough quality in the final third to break down an organised defence, making them favourites to claim all three points.

#1809. Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 7 November 2026

Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break.

There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation.

But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch.

If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot.

In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke.

The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise.

Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull

The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced

For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6)

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly

Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6)

Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz

For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition.

Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack.

It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull.

Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting.

Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend.

It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them.

Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious.

Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz

Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London

Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City.

Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors.

'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta.

'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that.

'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.'

Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy.

The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor.

Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position.

On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty.

'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it.

'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.'

The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick.

A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right?

Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective.

None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak.

Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour.

By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening.

First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner.

Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

#1808. Amorim discusses post-Genoa pride, the Ramos ‘team problem’ and losing being ‘end of the world’

Ruben Amorim wants his AC Milan side to fear losing, while he believes Goncalo Ramos’ lack of goals is a team problem.

Milan got their seventh win in 11 Serie A games on Sunday afternoon as they overcame an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Marassi. Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scored in the first half to put the Rossoneri in command, though Ellertsson’s late strike from range made it a nervy finish.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a result and a response that was needed after the dismal defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday night, and it calms some of the turbulence before the international break. However, the search to become consistently good side is one that will continue in a fortnight.

Amorim spoke to DAZN not long after the final whistle to give his assessments on what was an important win for his side but one that they made hard work of in the end, with his words via MilanNews.

A response was expected after the Europa League, and it arrived. But it’s only the beginning. What positive things do you take away from this?

“I’m proud of my players. The most important thing was to be competitive, I said it before the match. If we approach every game like this, we’re one step closer to winning them all.

“There are times when you manage to play really well, but there are also times when we changed our approach and were strong on second balls and played a different kind of football. And that’s what great teams do: they play differently within the same game. I’m really pleased with my players today.”

“What I can say is that we can win every game, but I can’t guarantee we’ll reach that level of confidence by the end of the season. I don’t feel like we’ve got that kind of consistency yet.

“And I don’t want to say anything more than ‘we can win the next game’. Because that’s the feeling I get when I look at the team. But it depends on many things. If we’d had everyone available, we would definitely have been better in the Europa League, too.

“This run of matches has been tough for us with everything that’s happened. But I can say that if we’re competitive, then we can win every game in the league. Let’s focus on that and take it one day at a time.”

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like you did on Thursday and then turn on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

How is Gonçalo Ramos’ development going? He got an assist today…

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1807. Harry Kane makes Will Lankshear admission as England handed clear striker succession plan

Harry Kane admits it would be great to work with Middlesbrough and England striker Will Lankshear, but added he did not want to put pressure on the young forward.

Lankshear has been in scintillating form since leaving Kane’s former club Tottenham for Championship high-flyers Middlesbrough over the summer, scoring 15 goals in 16 games in all competitions to spark calls for him to earn his first senior England call-up.

The 21-year-old was in contention for selection for England’s Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain this week, but did not make the cut, before pulling out of selection for the U21s with a muscular injury.

Lankshear’s form has been hard to miss this season, and Kane says that while the decision ultimately lies with Thomas Tuchel, he believes Lankshear would learn a lot from the attackers around him if he were called up to the senior team.

“I wouldn’t say I’ve followed his whole career. Obviously, this season it’s been hard not to hear about him, and he’s done extremely well at Middlesbrough,” Kane said at Tottenham’s training ground on Wednesday. afternoon.

“I’ve spoken to a friend of mine who coached him here (Tottenham) at the younger age group and said that he’s a goal scorer. He knows how to score. He’s in the right place at the right time. He’s a great finisher.

“We talk about a striker sometimes as having that goal-scoring instinct, and I think he’s one of those players for sure. He’s still early in his development. I think what he’s doing right now is perfect for him. Playing loads of games, scoring goals, getting confidence.

“Whether he comes into the senior side is down to Thomas. If he did, I’m sure he’d learn loads here, surrounded by the attackers that we have.”

The question of who will succeed 33-year-old Kane when he eventually hangs up his boots has gathered pace over the last year, with England not having a wealth of options to cover for the Bayern forward.

Kane and 29-year-old Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin are the only out-and-out strikers in England’s squad currently, but Kane admits that while he knows Tuchel will begin succession planning for him in the near future, Lankshear should be left to develop in his own time, free from external pressure.

“It’s not a time to put too much pressure on him. I know there’s a lot of talk about who’s going to replace me when I’m not here anymore, but just let him do what he’s doing,” Kane continued.
